### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

dbt-oss 2.0.5 accepts `--event-time-start` and `--event-time-end` on build, run and compile, but the values never reach Jinja:

- `invocation_args_dict` has no `event_time_start` or `event_time_end` key at all.
- `flags.EVENT_TIME_START` and `flags.EVENT_TIME_END` are empty.
- The `DBT_EVENT_TIME_START` / `DBT_EVENT_TIME_END` env vars behave the same way.

This happens both while dbt reads the project (`execute=False`) and while it compiles the model (`execute=True`). Only `invocation_args_dict.invocation_command` still contains the raw flags.

Macros that read the window from `invocation_args_dict` get nothing back, so a backfill run silently becomes a normal incremental run.

### Expected Behavior

As in dbt-core 1.12, `invocation_args_dict.event_time_start` and `invocation_args_dict.event_time_end` hold the values passed on the command line, for example `2026-09-01 00:00:00`.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a project with one model, models/probe.sql:
```
{{ print("start=" ~ invocation_args_dict.event_time_start ~ " end=" ~ invocation_args_dict.event_time_end) }}
{{ print("flags=" ~ flags.EVENT_TIME_START) }}
{{ print("keys=" ~ (invocation_args_dict.keys() | list | sort | join(","))) }}
select 1 as x
```
2. Run:
```
dbt compile --event-time-start 2026-09-01 --event-time-end 2026-09-03
```
`compile` needs no warehouse connection, so a dummy Databricks profile is enough.
 
3. The printed `start` and `end` values are empty, and `keys` has no `event_time_*` entry.
4. For comparison, run dbt-core 1.12.3 with `dbt run --event-time-start 2026-09-01 --event-time-end 2026-09-03`; 1.12 rejects these flags on `compile`. It prints `start=2026-09-01 00:00:00 end=2026-09-03 00:00:00`, and `keys` includes `event_time_start` and `event_time_end`.

### Relevant log output

```shell
dbt-oss 2.0.5:

PROBE execute=False start= end=
PROBE keys=debug,defer,defer_state,empty,favor_state,full_refresh,indirect_selection,introspect,invocation_command,invocation_id,log_format,log_format_file,log_level,log_level_file,log_path,num_threads,printer_width,profile,profiles_dir,project_dir,quiet,replay,resource_type,send_anonymous_usage_stats,store_failures,target,target_path,use_v2_compatible_package_downloads,vars,version_check,warn_error,warn_error_options,which,write_json
PROBE execute=True start= end=


dbt-core 1.12.3:

PROBE execute=False start=2026-09-01 00:00:00 end=2026-09-03 00:00:00
PROBE keys=...,event_time_end,event_time_start,...
```

### Environment

```markdown
- dbt: dbt-oss 2.0.5, with dbt-core 1.12.3 + dbt-databricks 1.12.5 for the comparison
- Adapter: Databricks
- OS: macOS (26.7)
- Python: 3.12
```

### Which database adapter are you using?

databricks

### Is this a discrepancy vs. dbt 1.x?

- [x] Yes — this works in dbt 1.x but not in dbt v2.x

### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

### Current Behavior

### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

Our Snowflake account locator contains an underscore (pattern: `my_org.eu-central-1`). With `authenticator: externalbrowser`, dbt v2 (2.0.6, Rust driver `snowflake 0.21.0.dev+dbt0.21.18`) cannot establish a connection:

- With the underscore spelling in profiles.yml (`account: my_org.eu-central-1`), the driver requests `https://my-org.eu-central-1.snowflakecomputing.com/session/authenticator-request` (note the underscore already replaced by a hyphen in the URL) and gets HTTP 404. The VS Code extension surfaces this as:

  ```
  [DbConnectionFailed (dbt1300)]: [Snowflake] 261005 (08004): failed to auth via SAML for unknown reason.
  HTTP: 404, URL: https://my-org.eu-central-1.snowflakecomputing.com:443/session/authenticator-request?requestId=...
  ```

  On the CLI the same command does NOT surface the error: it hangs silently (connect_timeout 600 x connect_retries 3 = up to 30 minutes with no output after "Started downloading schemas").

- With the hyphen spelling (`account: my-org.eu-central-1`), the browser SAML flow completes (IdP shows "Your identity was confirmed and propagated to Snowflake dbt"), but the session login after the callback then hangs indefinitely; `dbt debug` never finishes.

dbt Core 1.12.5 with the Python connector connects fine with the underscore spelling from the same machine in about 5 seconds (`dbt debug` = "All checks passed"), as do DBeaver (JDBC) and the Snowflake Python connector directly. Both hostname spellings answer HTTP 302 on `https://<host>/`, so DNS resolves either way.

### Expected Behavior

Same behavior as the Python connector: externalbrowser auth succeeds for an account locator containing an underscore. Independently of the root cause, a connection-level auth failure should be reported as an error on the CLI instead of hanging silently in the retry loop.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Snowflake account whose locator contains an underscore, region-qualified (e.g. `my_org.eu-central-1`).
2. profiles.yml with `type: snowflake`, `authenticator: externalbrowser`, that account.
3. `dbt debug` on dbt 2.0.6 (windows x86_64): hangs; VS Code extension shows dbt1300 with HTTP 404 on /session/authenticator-request.
4. Same profile with dbt Core 1.12.5: connects successfully.

### Relevant log output

```shell

[DbConnectionFailed (dbt1300)]: [Snowflake] 261005 (08004): failed to auth via SAML for unknown reason.
HTTP: 404, URL: https://my-org.eu-central-1.snowflakecomputing.com:443/session/authenticator-request?requestId=e6616b76-f19c-4a2b-4ac6-7452be982343


**CLI `dbt compile` stdout (same profile) - last line ever printed, then silence:**

   Started resolving packages from packages.yml
  Finished [  0.28s] resolving packages from packages.yml (4 items)

**logs/dbt.log for that invocation - the last entries, no error is ever logged:**


07:43:00.164488 [info ]: Started downloading schemas
07:43:00.164525 [info ]:    Started downloading schemas (64 items)
07:43:00.165041 [debug]: Snowflake driver resolved: snowflake 0.21.0.dev+dbt0.21.18
(nothing further; process still alive 20+ minutes later, killed manually)


**`dbt debug` stdout with the HYPHEN spelling - browser SAML flow completes ("Your identity was confirmed and propagated to Snowflake dbt"), then hangs after printing the connection config:**


 Debugging connection:
  "client_session_keep_alive": true,
  "connect_retries": 3,
  "connect_timeout": 600,
  "reuse_connections": true,
  "authenticator": "externalbrowser",
  "account": "my-org.eu-central-1",
  "user": "user@example.com",
  "database": "MY_DB",
  "warehouse": "MY_WH",
  "schema": "MY_SCHEMA",
  "role": "MY_ROLE"
(no "connection test" line ever appears; killed after 6 minutes)


**Control: dbt Core 1.12.5, same profile, underscore spelling:**


Initiating login request with your identity provider. Press CTRL+C to abort and try again...
Going to open: https://logon.okta.com/app/snowflake/.../sso/saml?SAMLRequest=... to authenticate...
  Connection test: [OK connection ok]
All checks passed!
```

### Environment

```markdown
- IdP: Okta (SAML/externalbrowser)

```

snowflake

issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

To run a UDF locally, local compute rewrites its body into a macro and inlines the call as a correlated subquery, binding the parameters through a `VALUES` clause:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO concat_7ee27d0f(arg0) AS (list_reduce(arg0, lambda x, y : x || y));

(SELECT concat_7ee27d0f(IN_A, 'x')
 FROM (SELECT "col0" AS IN_A FROM VALUES ('a')))
```

If a UDF calls a variadic built-in function (e.g. `CONCAT`, `GREATEST`), note that the generated macro expects a list, while the unit test SQL invokes the macro with individual arguments, causing an error.

### Expected Behavior

Generated unit test SQL for UDFs calling variadic built-ins packs function arguments into list to conform to macro definition.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a UDF calling a variadic built-in function, model, and unit test
```sql
-- functions/fn_concat.sql
CONCAT(in_a, 'x')
```
```yml
# functions/schema.yml
functions:
  - name: fn_concat
    config:
      schema: <schema>
      database: <db>
      volatility: deterministic
    arguments:
      - name: in_a
        data_type: varchar
    returns:
      data_type: varchar
```
```sql
-- models/variadic_builtin_in_udf_body.sql
SELECT
    {{ function('fn_concat') }}('a') AS concat_result
```
```yml
unit_tests:
  - name: test_variadic_builtin_in_udf_body
    config:
      compute: local
    model: variadic_builtin_in_udf_body
    expect:
      rows:
        - { concat_result: "ax" }
```

2. Run `dbt build -s +variadic_builtin_in_udf_body` and observe error
```
================================================================================================== Errors and Warnings ==================================================================================================
[error] [DbConnectionFailed (dbt1300)]: Unit test <snip>.test_variadic_builtin_in_udf_body in db_runner: Internal: Binder Error: Macro concat_7ee27d0f() does not support the supplied arguments. You might need to add explicit type casts.
Candidate macros:
        concat_7ee27d0f(arg0)

LINE 1: ...ESULT, 'actual' AS ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED FROM (SELECT (SELECT concat_7ee27d0f(IN_A, 'x') FROM (SELECT "col0" AS IN_A FROM...
                                                                      ^ (sqlstate: [0, 0, 0, 0, 0], vendor_code: -2147483648)
```


### Environment

```markdown
- OS: Ubuntu
- CPU: (x86 or ARM) x86
- dbt distribution and version: (`dbt --version`) 2.0.7
```

snowflake

issues.title: Fusion: catalogs.yml type: ducklake with Postgres metadata_path — writes succeed silently but are never committed to the metastore
issues.body:
## Summary

Configuring a DuckLake catalog in `catalogs.yml` with a Postgres-backed `metadata_path` appears to work: `dbt run` reports success and executes the expected DDL against the named catalog. But the changes are never actually committed as a new DuckLake snapshot in the Postgres metastore — a fresh, independent `ATTACH` to the same Postgres database cannot find the table, and `ducklake_snapshot.next_file_id` never advances past its initial value.

This makes `catalogs.yml` + `type: ducklake` + a Postgres-backed `metadata_path` unsafe today: `dbt run` reports success while silently not persisting anything to the real catalog.

## Environment

- dbt (Fusion) 2.0.6, macOS x86_64
- DuckDB `ducklake` extension (bundled with the Fusion binary)
- PostgreSQL 18 (Docker) as the DuckLake metadata backend

## Repro steps

`dbt_project.yml`:
```yaml
name: catalogs_check2
version: '1.0.0'
profile: catalogs_check2
model-paths: ["models"]
flags:
  use_catalogs_v2: true
```

`catalogs.yml`:
```yaml
catalogs:
  - name: clean_lake
    type: ducklake
    table_format: default
    config:
      duckdb:
        metadata_path: "dbname=ducklake_clean host=localhost port=5432 user=postgres password=test"
        data_path: "/tmp/data"
```

`profiles/profiles.yml`:
```yaml
catalogs_check2:
  target: dev
  outputs:
    dev:
      type: duckdb
      path: ':memory:'
```

`models/m1.sql`:
```sql
{{ config(materialized='table', catalog_name='clean_lake') }}
select 42 as answer
```

Run against a **completely fresh, empty** Postgres database (`CREATE DATABASE ducklake_clean;`, nothing else):
```
dbt run
```

## Expected

The `m1` table is created and its DuckLake snapshot metadata is committed to the Postgres metastore — a fresh `ATTACH 'ducklake:postgres:<same dsn>'` from a separate process can see the table.

## Actual

`dbt run` reports:
```
Succeeded model main.m1 (table) [1 of 1 in 0.18s]
```

`logs/query_log.sql` confirms it executed real DDL against the correct, named catalog:
```sql
create schema if not exists "clean_lake"."main";

create table "clean_lake"."main"."m1__dbt_tmp" as (select 42 as answer);

alter table "clean_lake"."main"."m1__dbt_tmp" rename to "m1";

drop table if exists "clean_lake"."main"."m1__dbt_backup";
```

But inspecting the Postgres metastore directly afterwards:
- `ducklake_schema` has one row (`main`) — schema registration worked.
- `ducklake_table` is **empty** — the table was never registered.
- `ducklake_snapshot` has only the initial row; `next_file_id`/`next_catalog_id` never advance past their starting values.

A completely independent DuckDB session run afterward —
```sql
ATTACH 'ducklake:postgres:dbname=ducklake_clean host=localhost port=5432 user=postgres password=test' AS lake (DATA_PATH '/tmp/data/');
SELECT * FROM lake.main.m1;
```
— confirms `lake.main.m1` does not exist.

**Reproduced twice, on two separate, fully fresh Postgres databases**, to rule out leftover state from earlier tests.

## Additional notes

- `metadata_path` does accept a plain Postgres DSN string (`dbname=... host=... port=... user=... password=...`) for `config.duckdb` — this isn't documented anywhere I could find ([catalogs.yml docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/iceberg/catalogs-yml) and the [DuckDB blog announcement](https://duckdb.org/2026/09/22/dbt-fusion) only show a local-file `metadata_path` example), so it took some trial and error to even confirm the DSN format is accepted at all. Might be worth documenting explicitly once this bug is fixed.
- I noticed (via `strings` on the compiled binary) two config keys that look relevant but are undocumented: `automatic_migration` and `create_if_not_exists` under `config.duckdb`. Adding them to `catalogs.yml` seemed to prevent even the schema-level Postgres tables from being created at all — I didn't dig further into why, could be a separate issue or user error on my part.
- I tried working around this with an explicit `post_hook="CALL ducklake_commit('clean_lake')"`. The function exists (DuckDB suggested it when I first tried the nonexistent `ducklake_checkpoint`), but it requires a `snapshot_id` plus retry parameters that aren't documented for this simple "just flush now" use case, so I didn't pursue a manual-commit workaround further.
- I suspect this may share a root cause with #15758 (temp tables not surviving between `run_query` calls on Fusion+DuckDB, reported against Fusion 2.0.0-preview.204). If each SQL statement in a model run goes through a separate/reset DuckDB connection rather than one persistent session for the whole run, that would plausibly explain why the DuckLake snapshot — which likely needs to be finalized against one continuous session/transaction — never gets committed here either. I haven't verified this connection-reset theory directly against this specific repro, just noting the similarity.

Happy to share the full isolated repro project if useful.

issues.title: [VSCE] [Bug] "Show column lineage" returns "No columns found" for any model that refs a seed, and for its downstream models
issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in the VS Code extension?
- [x] I believe this is a new bug in the VS Code extension, not the dbt Fusion CLI
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior
With `static_analysis: strict`, **dbt: View Lineage → Show column lineage** shows "No columns found..." for any model that `ref()`s a seed, and for every model downstream of it.

The language server returns `"columns": {}` from `dbt.getCurrentNode` for these models, although it logs them as successfully analyzed. The CLI produces column lineage for the same models.

In our project this affects 76 of 144 models.

### Expected Behavior
The column picker lists the model's columns, as it does for models that don't depend on a seed, and as `dbt compile --static-analysis strict --generate-info-schema` reports in `dbt.column_lineage.parquet`.

### Troubleshooting
- Consistent. Survives `Developer: Reload Window` and deleting `target/.lsp`.
- Reading the seed's table through `source()` instead of `ref()` makes the columns appear.
- `+column_types` on the seed does not help.

### Steps To Reproduce
Minimal project (any Snowflake profile; the seed does not need to be loaded):

`dbt_project.yml`
```yaml
name: seed_lineage_repro
version: "1.0.0"
profile: default
models:
  seed_lineage_repro:
    +static_analysis: strict
    +materialized: view
```

`seeds/my_seed.csv`
```csv
id,name
1,a
2,b
```

`models/from_seed.sql`
```sql
select id, name from {{ ref('my_seed') }}
```

`models/downstream_of_seed.sql`
```sql
select id, upper(name) as name_upper from {{ ref('from_seed') }}
```

`models/no_seed.sql` (control)
```sql
select 1 as id, 'a' as name
```

1. Open the project in VS Code with the dbt extension and let the background compile finish.
2. Right-click `models/from_seed.sql` → **dbt: View Lineage → Show column lineage**: "No columns found...".

issues.title: [v2 Bug] [Local Compute] Incorrect unit test SQL generated by `dbt test -s model` compared to `dbt build -s +model`

issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

When unit testing the expected vs. actual output from a `given` column, `dbt test -s` and `dbt build +s` generate different unit test SQL. In several cases, `dbt test -s` SQL is incorrect, including
- incorrect truncation of decimal scale
- incorrect VARIANT / VARCHAR casting when testing VARIANT columns
- syntactically incorrect test SQL when testing UDFs on input columns

In the example below, note that `dbt test -s` generates the `expected` fixture with the data type `DECIMAL(38, 0)`, even though the model's column type is `DECIMAL(38, 2).
```sql
            SELECT
                "<snip>_decimal_expect".DECIMAL_COL,
                'expected' AS ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
            FROM
                (SELECT TRY_CAST('42.78' AS DECIMAL(38, 0)) AS DECIMAL_COL)
                    AS "<snip>_decimal_expect"
        )
```

### Expected Behavior

`dbt test -s` produces valid unit test SQL

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create models and unit test.
```sql
-- expected_decimal_stub.sql
SELECT CAST(NULL AS NUMBER(38, 2)) AS decimal_col
```
```sql
-- expected_decimal.sql
SELECT decimal_col + 1
FROM {{ ref('expected_decimal_stub') }}
```
```yml
unit_tests:
  - name: test_expected_decimal
    config:
        compute: local
    model: expected_decimal
    given:
      - input: ref('expected_decimal_stub')
        rows:
          - { decimal_col: 41.78 }
    expect:
      rows:
        - { decimal_col: 42.78 }
```
2. Run `dbt run -s +expected_decimal` and `dbt test -s expected_decimal`, observe failure.
```
┌───────────────┐
│ DECIMAL_COL   │
╞═══════════════╡
│ 43.0 -> 42.78 │
└───────────────┘
```
generated `dbt test -s` SQL:
```sql
SELECT
    UNIT_TEST_DIFF.DECIMAL_COL,
    UNIT_TEST_DIFF.ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
FROM (
    SELECT
        DECIMAL_COL,
        ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
    FROM (
        SELECT
            "<snip>_decimal_actual".DECIMAL_COL,
            'actual' AS ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
        FROM
            (
                SELECT
                    CAST(("<snip>_stub".DECIMAL_COL + 1) AS DECIMAL(38, 2))
                        AS DECIMAL_COL
                FROM
                    (
                        SELECT TRY_CAST('41.78' AS DECIMAL(38, 2)) AS DECIMAL_COL
                    ) AS "<snip>_stub"
            ) AS "<snip>_decimal_actual"
        UNION ALL
        SELECT
            CAST(DECIMAL_COL AS DECIMAL(38, 2)) AS DECIMAL_COL,
            ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
        FROM (
            SELECT
                "<snip>_decimal_expect".DECIMAL_COL,
                'expected' AS ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
            FROM
                (SELECT TRY_CAST('42.78' AS DECIMAL(38, 0)) AS DECIMAL_COL)
                    AS "<snip>_decimal_expect"
        )
    )
) AS UNIT_TEST_DIFF
ORDER BY UNIT_TEST_DIFF.DECIMAL_COL ASC NULLS LAST;
```
3. Run `dbt build -s +expected_decimal` and observe pass.
generated `dbt build -s +` SQL:
```sql

    UNIT_TEST_DIFF.DECIMAL_COL,
    UNIT_TEST_DIFF.ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
FROM (
    SELECT
        DECIMAL_COL,
        ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
    FROM (
        SELECT
            "<snip>_decimal_actual".DECIMAL_COL,
            'actual' AS ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
        FROM
            (
                SELECT
                    CAST(("<snip>_stub".DECIMAL_COL + 1) AS DECIMAL(38, 2))
                        AS DECIMAL_COL
                FROM
                    (
                        SELECT TRY_CAST('41.78' AS DECIMAL(38, 2)) AS DECIMAL_COL
                    ) AS "<snip>_stub"
            ) AS "<snip>_decimal_actual"
        UNION ALL
        SELECT
            "<snip>_decimal_expect".DECIMAL_COL,
            'expected' AS ACTUAL_OR_EXPECTED
        FROM
            (SELECT TRY_CAST('42.78' AS DECIMAL(38, 2)) AS DECIMAL_COL)
                AS "<snip>_decimal_expect"
    )
) AS UNIT_TEST_DIFF
ORDER BY UNIT_TEST_DIFF.DECIMAL_COL ASC NULLS LAST;
```

issues.title: [v2 Bug] Unit test macro override on a package-qualified macro makes the rest of that package undefined

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: A defect: Fusion behaves incorrectly versus expected/reference behavior.

labels.name: area:adapters
labels.description: The adapter framework/layer connecting Fusion to warehouses (dbt-adapter* crates).

issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

When a unit test overrides a package-qualified macro, e.g. `my_project.is_ci`, every other macro in that package becomes undefined for the test. Calling any of them fails with `value of type undefined is not callable`.

This happens even when the overridden macro is never called, and it happens for the root project's own namespace too, not just installed packages.

### Expected Behavior

Only the overridden macro should be stubbed. Other macros in the package should still resolve, and macros that call the overridden one should see the stub. That's how dbt 1.11 behaves.


### Steps To Reproduce

Repro project: https://github.com/phil-baines-insta/dbt-fusion-issue/tree/main/unit_test_macro_overrides

1. `my_project` has two macros: `is_ci()` returns false, and `pick_label()` returns `'ci'` if `my_project.is_ci()` is true, otherwise `'local'`.
2. Model `label.sql`: `select '{{ my_project.pick_label() }}'::varchar as result`
3. Add a unit test that overrides the macro:

```yaml
unit_tests:
  - name: same_project__override_called_macro
    model: label
    overrides:
      macros:
        my_project.is_ci: true
    given: []
    expect:
      rows:
        - {result: ci}
```

4. Run `dbt build` in `my_project`. The test fails on 2.0.6 and passes on 1.11.6.

The repo also has a nested `integration_tests` project that installs `my_project` with `local: ..` and hits the same error.

### Relevant log output

```shell
Failed unit_test same_project__override_called_macro (models/label.yml:11:11)
Failed unit_test same_project__override_unrelated_macro (models/label.yml:22:11)
Passed unit_test same_project__no_override

[error] [JinjaError (dbt1501)]: Failed to render SQL invalid operation: value of type undefined is not callable
(in models/label.yml:1:9)


The error location is also wrong. Line 1, col 9 is the `my_project.pick_label()` call in `label.sql`, not anything in `label.yml`.
```

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: macOS 26.5
- CPU: ARM (Apple Silicon)
- dbt distribution and version: dbt 2.0.6
```

### Which database adapter are you using?

snowflake

### Is this a discrepancy vs. dbt 1.x?

- [x] Yes — this works in dbt 1.x but not in dbt v2.x

### Additional Context

Links are to the `v2.0.5` tag, the newest tag on this repo. This code hasn't changed since May, so I assume 2.0.6 is the same.

I think the cause is in how unit test overrides are merged into the package namespace:

1. [`bind_override_macros`](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt/blob/v2.0.5/crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/renderable/renderable/unit_test.rs#L894-L925) handles `pkg.macro` overrides. It [wraps the existing namespace](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt/blob/v2.0.5/crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/renderable/renderable/unit_test.rs#L913-L915) in an `ObjectOverlay`, with the stub first and the real namespace second.
2. [`ObjectOverlay::get_value`](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt/blob/v2.0.5/crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/renderable/renderable/unit_test.rs#L174-L182) is supposed to fall through to the real namespace when the stub doesn't have the key. It relies on `get_item` returning an error for a missing key (the comment there says "Err if undefined").
3. But [`Value::get_item`](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt/blob/v2.0.5/crates/dbt-jinja/minijinja/src/value/mod.rs#L1458-L1464) returns `Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)` for a missing key. It only errors when the value it's called on is undefined.

So the stub always answers first, and every non-overridden macro in the package comes back undefined.

Possible fix:

```rust
self.0
    .iter()
    .find_map(|o| o.get_item_opt(key).filter(|v| !v.is_undefined()))
```

issues.title: [PORT-OVER] Stage V1 Databricks view replacements of non-view relations
issues.body:
Port of https://github.com/databricks/dbt-databricks/pull/1688.

With `use_materialization_v2` off (the default), a Databricks view model that replaces an existing table or other non-view relation drops that relation before creating the view. If the view fails to build, the run fails and the table is gone.

dbt-databricks#1688 routes that case through `get_replace_sql`, the replacement flow the V2 view path already uses: the view is built at a staging relation and swapped in only after it succeeds, so a failed build keeps the existing table.

Fusion's vendored `dbt-databricks/macros/materializations/view.sql` still has the drop-first V1 branch.

issues.title: [Fusion] CLI --vars replaces dbt_project.yml vars instead of merging
issues.body:
### Which engine
dbt Fusion 2.0.6

### Summary
Passing `--vars` on the CLI makes `dbt_project.yml` top-level `vars:` **unavailable** — `var('x')` for a project-defined `x` raises `[JinjaError (dbt1501)]: Required var 'x' not found in config`, even though `x` is defined in `dbt_project.yml`. In dbt-core, CLI `--vars` **merge with and override** project vars; Fusion appears to **replace** them.

### Repro
`dbt_project.yml`:
```yaml
vars:
  my_project_var: 40
```
A model uses `{{ var('my_project_var') }}`. Then:
```
dbt build --select that_model --vars '{"something_else": true}'
```
→ `Required var 'my_project_var' not found in config` (it's defined in the project; only present because the CLI `--vars` didn't list it).
Without `--vars`, it resolves fine.

### Expected
CLI `--vars` merges over project `vars:` (project vars remain available unless explicitly overridden) — matching dbt-core behavior.

### Impact
Any workflow that passes `--vars` for one override silently loses every `dbt_project.yml` var, breaking model configs like `config(snowflake_warehouse=var('medium_warehouse'))`. Migrating existing projects to Fusion breaks builds that were relying on the documented merge semantics.

issues.title: [v2 Bug] Databricks: views fail with 'materialized must be incremental, table, or seed' under an iceberg catalog in catalogs.yml v2

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: A defect: Fusion behaves incorrectly versus expected/reference behavior.

labels.name: area:adapters
labels.description: The adapter framework/layer connecting Fusion to warehouses (dbt-adapter* crates).

labels.name: adapter:databricks
labels.description: Concerns the Databricks adapter / SQL dialect.

labels.name: proj:catalog-v2
labels.description: Catalog v2 initiative (Iceberg, catalogs, table-format support).

issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

On Databricks with catalogs.yml **v2** (`use_catalogs_v2`, which now defaults to `true`), a view that resolves to a catalog with `table_format: iceberg` fails to build:

```
[error] [InvalidConfig (dbt1005)]: Error executing materialization macro 'dbt_databricks.materialization_view_databricks' for model model.<project>.<view_model>: Configuration Error: When table_format is 'iceberg', materialized must be 'incremental', 'table', or 'seed'.
```

In v2, projects commonly set `+catalog_name` for a whole folder or project. Every model under it, **including views**, then inherits the catalog's `table_format`. The model can't override `table_format` in v2, so there's no valid way to build a view under an iceberg catalog, short of setting `catalog_name: none` on every view.

### Expected Behavior

A view has no storage format, so Iceberg/UniForm doesn't apply to it. A view routed to an iceberg catalog should build as a normal view (no UniForm tblproperties) instead of raising a configuration error.

### Steps To Reproduce

`catalogs.yml` (v2):

```yaml
catalogs:
  - name: my_uc
    type: unity
    table_format: iceberg
    config:
      databricks:
        file_format: delta
        use_uniform: true
```

`dbt_project.yml`:

```yaml
models:
  my_project:
    +catalog_name: my_uc
```

`models/my_view.sql`:

```sql
{{ config(materialized='view') }}
select 1 as id
```

Run `dbt build -s my_view` against Databricks. It fails with the error above.

### Root cause

1. `catalog_relation_v2.rs` (`build_databricks_unity_with_catalogs_v2`) sets `table_format = catalog.table_format` unconditionally. In v2 the model can't override it, whereas in v1 `build_databricks_with_catalogs` let the model's `table_format` take precedence.
2. `databricks__create_view_as` → `tblproperties_clause()` → `adapter.is_uniform(config)`. `is_uniform` (`adapter_impl.rs`) raises for any iceberg relation whose `materialized` isn't `incremental`, `table` or `seed`. `view/alter.sql` reaches the same check via `apply_tblproperties` when `view_update_via_alter` is set.

The check itself matches upstream dbt-databricks. Upstream (and Fusion v1) lets a view avoid it by overriding `table_format` per model; v2 removed that option without relaxing the check. Flipping the `use_catalogs_v2` default turned this into a dead end for existing projects.

### Proposed fix

In `is_uniform`, when catalogs v2 is active and `materialized == view`, return `false` before the DBR version check and the materialization check. This keeps v1 behavior matching upstream, and it covers both the create path and the alter path.

### Workaround

Override the dispatched macro in the root project so views skip the UniForm branch:

```jinja
{% macro databricks__tblproperties_clause(tblproperties=None) -%}
  {%- if config.get('materialized') == 'view' -%}
    {%- set tblproperties = tblproperties or config.get("tblproperties", {}) -%}
  {%- elif adapter.is_uniform(config) -%}
    {%- set tblproperties = adapter.update_tblproperties_for_uniform_iceberg(config, tblproperties) -%}
  {%- else -%}
    {%- set tblproperties = tblproperties or config.get("tblproperties", {}) -%}
  {%- endif -%}
  {%- if tblproperties != {} %}
    tblproperties (
      {%- for prop in tblproperties -%}
      '{{ prop }}' = '{{ tblproperties[prop] }}' {% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}
      {%- endfor %}
    )
  {%- endif %}
{%- endmacro -%}
```

### Environment

- dbt v2.x (Fusion), Databricks adapter, Unity Catalog
- catalogs.yml v2 (default `use_catalogs_v2: true`)

### Which database adapter are you using?

Databricks

### Is this a discrepancy vs. dbt 1.x?

Partially. dbt 1.x / upstream dbt-databricks has the same check, but there a view can avoid it by overriding `table_format` per model. catalogs.yml v2 removes that option.

### Additional Context

Reported by a customer with a broad iceberg catalog assignment where most tables have an associated view, so per-model changes aren't practical.

issues.title: [Fusion] OTEL telemetry omits the --full-refresh flag (no full_refresh in Invocation eval_args)
issues.body:
### Which engine
dbt Fusion 2.0.6

### Summary
Fusion's native OTEL telemetry does not record whether a run was a full-refresh. Running with `--full-refresh` produces an `Invocation` event whose `eval_args` has no `full_refresh` key, and no full-refresh indicator appears anywhere else in the emitted payload (checked `Invocation` and node events).

### Repro
```
dbt run --select <any_model> --full-refresh --otel-parquet-file-name out.parquet
```
Inspect the `v1.public.events.fusion.invocation.Invocation` event → attributes → `json_payload` → `eval_args`.

### Expected
`eval_args` (or a per-node field) reflects that `--full-refresh` was passed — analogous to dbt-core's `dbt.full_refresh_flag` / per-node `dbt.model.was_full_refresh`.

### Actual
`eval_args` keys are exactly: `command, debug, limit, log_format, manage_state, quiet, resource_types, select, vars, write_catalog, write_json`. No `full_refresh` anywhere in the payload, with or without the flag.

### Impact
Downstream OTEL consumers can't distinguish full-refresh from incremental runs. dbt-core (dbt_artifacts/otel export) emitted this, so migrating telemetry to Fusion loses the signal — e.g. a Honeycomb dashboard splitting dbt run metrics by full-refresh vs incremental can no longer populate the full-refresh view.

### Note
Filed here because `dbt-labs/dbt-fusion` has issues disabled; please redirect if there's a better home for Fusion engine issues.

issues.title: [v2 Bug] dapter.get_columns_in_relation() throws ExecutorFailed (dbt1401) on Databricks for a nonexistent relation, instead of returning []

### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

On Databricks, calling `adapter.get_columns_in_relation()` against a relation that does not exist raises `[ExecutorFailed (dbt1401)]: Unexpected Result: Unexpected result type ()` instead of returning an empty list.

In practice this surfaces as a `dbt compile` failure: `dbt compile` renders every model's Jinja without ever creating anything, so any model whose SQL calls `adapter.get_columns_in_relation(ref(...))` on an upstream relation that hasn't been built yet triggers this crash during introspection.

### Expected Behavior

`adapter.get_columns_in_relation()` should return an empty list (`[]`) when called against a relation that does not exist, matching dbt-core v1's behavior, and matching dbt v2's own behavior on Snowflake, BigQuery, and DuckDB (all tested with the same `dbt-oss` 2.0.5 binary).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Add this macro to a project targeting Databricks:

```jinja
{% macro zzz_debug_repro() %}
  {% set target_relation = api.Relation.create(
      database=target.database,
      schema=target.schema,
      identifier='zzz_definitely_does_not_exist_anywhere'
  ) %}
  {% set existing = adapter.get_relation(database=target_relation.database, schema=target_relation.schema, identifier=target_relation.identifier) %}
  {{ log("get_relation returned: " ~ existing, info=true) }}
  {% set cols = adapter.get_columns_in_relation(target_relation) %}
  {{ log("columns: " ~ cols, info=true) }}
{% endmacro %}
```

2. Run `dbt run-operation zzz_debug_repro --target databricks`

### Relevant log output

```shell
Actual (Databricks):


get_relation returned: None
[error] [ExecutorFailed (dbt1401)]: Unexpected Result: Unexpected result type ()


Expected (matches Snowflake, BigQuery, DuckDB):


get_relation returned: None
columns: []
```

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: macOS (Darwin), also reproduced from Linux CI (Ubuntu 24.04, amd64)
- CPU: ARM (Apple Silicon)
- dbt distribution and version: dbt-oss 2.0.5
```

### Which database adapter are you using?

databricks

### Is this a discrepancy vs. dbt 1.x?

- [x] Yes — this works in dbt 1.x but not in dbt v2.x

Adapters tested (same `dbt-oss` 2.0.5 binary, only `--target` changed):

issues.title: [v2 Bug] DuckDB unit test fixtures cast TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE columns as `timestamp without time zone`, shifting values by the session timezone

labels.name: area:adapters
labels.description: The adapter framework/layer connecting Fusion to warehouses (dbt-adapter* crates).

issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

For a model column of type `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`, the `expect` fixture value is cast as `timestamp without time zone` in the generated unit test SQL (`target/compiled/<project>/models/<test>.sql`):

```sql
CAST('2024-01-01 00:00:00+00' AS timestamp without time zone) AS ts_tz
```

The `+00` offset is dropped, and the `UNION ALL` with the actual column re-interprets the value in the session timezone. With `TimeZone = America/Sao_Paulo`, expected renders as `2024-01-01T00:00:00-03:00` while actual is `2023-12-31T21:00:00-03:00`, so a correct expectation is three hours off. With `TZ=UTC` the same test passes.

Today this is masked by #15894 (timestamp columns are never compared, both sides render as `[unsupported]`). Once that is fixed, correct tz-aware expectations fail on DuckDB outside UTC.

### Expected Behavior

The fixture should be cast to the column's actual type (`timestamp with time zone`) so `'2024-01-01 00:00:00+00'` keeps its offset and matches the model output in any session timezone. This is what dbt-core 1.12.5 with dbt-duckdb generates:

```sql
cast('2024-01-01 00:00:00+00' as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `models/ts_model.sql`:
   ```sql
   select timestamptz '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00' as ts_tz
   ```
2. `models/ts_model.yml`:
   ```yaml
   unit_tests:
     - name: tz_fixture_matches
       model: ts_model
       given: []
       expect:
         rows:
           - {ts_tz: "2024-01-01 00:00:00+00"}
   ```
3. DuckDB profile, session timezone other than UTC (for example `TZ=America/Sao_Paulo dbt build`).
4. Inspect `target/compiled/<project>/models/tz_fixture_matches.sql`: the expected CTE casts `ts_tz` as `timestamp without time zone`.
5. Re-run with `TZ=UTC dbt build` and compare.

### Relevant log output

With the comparison fix from #15894 applied locally, the diff table shows:

```
| ts_tz                                                  |
| 2024-01-01T00:00:00-03:00 -> 2023-12-31T21:00:00-03:00 |
```

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- CPU: ARM
- dbt distribution and version: dbt 2.0.6 (Core); OSS build from `main` at 7e4e937c4 for the diff output. Compared against dbt-core 1.12.5 + dbt-duckdb 1.11.0, where the same test passes.

### Which database adapter are you using?

duckdb

### Is this a discrepancy vs. dbt 1.x?

- [x] Yes — this works in dbt 1.x but not in dbt v2.x

### Additional Context

Cause: the type formatter in `crates/dbt-adapter/src/sql_types.rs` renders every `DataType::Timestamp(_, _)` as `timestamp without time zone`, ignoring the timezone on the Arrow type. Found while working on #15894; that fix does not change fixture typing.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The docs say BigQuery `biglake_metastore` catalogs using `lakehouse_catalog` (LRC / Lakehouse Runtime Catalog) don't need `external_volume` or `file_format`, since LRC derives storage location from the catalog/namespace registration:

> An LRC catalog doesn't need `external_volume` or `file_format`.

In practice, `catalogs.yml` validation rejects this and unconditionally requires both fields, even when `lakehouse_catalog` is set — so the documented minimal LRC example (`lakehouse_catalog` alone, no `external_volume`/`file_format`) fails to parse at all.

### Steps to reproduce

`catalogs.yml`:
```yaml
catalogs:
  - name: my_lrc_catalog
    type: biglake_metastore
    table_format: iceberg
    config:
      bigquery:
        lakehouse_catalog: sales_catalog
```

### Expected behavior

This config validates successfully, matching the documented LRC example.

### Actual behavior

```
[InvalidConfig (dbt1005)]: Catalog 'my_lrc_catalog' biglake_metastore/bigquery requires 'external_volume'
```

### Environment

- dbt Fusion 2.0.6
- BigQuery, `biglake_metastore` catalog with `lakehouse_catalog` (LRC) set

### Related

Related to (but distinct from) the empty-`OPTIONS()` bug tracked in #16464.

### Additional Context

I chatted with a Cursor agent about what the issue could be, and it said this:

>  264002 is the Go Snowflake driver's code for "failed to download from stage", so the GET itself is what's failing. 

> "cannot find executable path" is an error from Go's standard library on macOS. It happens when a program asks "where is my executable on disk?" (os.Executable()) and macOS doesn't provide an answer ([Go source](https://go.dev/src/os/executable_darwin.go)).

> Fusion/dbt V2 is written in Rust, but it talks to Snowflake through a Go driver loaded as a library inside the Rust binary. In that setup, Go often can't discover the executable path. Others have hit the same error in [Kitex](https://github.com/cloudwego/kitex/issues/1398) and [Tailscale](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/19050). Normal queries never ask for that path, but GET goes through a separate file-transfer code path that appears to. So the SQL gets through fine and the download to local disk fails.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Configuring a BigQuery `biglake_metastore` catalog with `lakehouse_catalog` set (Lakehouse Runtime Catalog / 4-part namespace support) causes Fusion to generate `CREATE TABLE` DDL with a completely empty `OPTIONS()` clause. BigQuery rejects the DDL:

```
BigLake config must have storage_uri specified when specifying managed_table_type='BIGLAKE'
```

### Steps to reproduce

`catalogs.yml`:
```yaml
catalogs:
  - name: lrc_iceberg
    type: biglake_metastore
    table_format: iceberg
    config:
      bigquery:
        external_volume: 'gs://my-bucket'
        file_format: parquet
        lakehouse_catalog: my-lakehouse-catalog
```

`dbt_project.yml`:
```yaml
flags:
  use_catalogs_v2: true
```

Run any model configured with this catalog.

### Expected behavior

The generated `OPTIONS()` still includes `storage_uri` and `file_format`. Only `table_format` (and the `with connection` clause) should be omitted for LRC tables.

### Actual behavior

```sql
create or replace table `project`.`catalog.schema`.`table`
with connection default OPTIONS()
```

An empty `OPTIONS()`, which BigQuery rejects outright.

### Environment

- dbt Fusion 2.0.6
- BigQuery, `biglake_metastore` catalog with `lakehouse_catalog` (LRC) set

issues.title: [Fusion] model.batch is a zero-width placeholder in the unit-test context (dbt-core leaves it None)
issues.body:
### Which engine

dbt **Fusion 2.0.6** vs dbt-core **1.11.12**, Snowflake adapter.

### Summary

When compiling a `dbt unit test` for a **microbatch** model, Fusion sets `model.batch` to a **non-None object whose `event_time_start == event_time_end`** (observed `2025-01-01 01:01:01+00:00` for both, `id=''`). dbt-core leaves `model.batch = None` outside actual microbatch execution (unit tests, `--empty`).

Model SQL that conditionally applies a manual batch filter based on `model.batch` therefore behaves differently between the engines. A guard like:

```jinja
{%- if model.batch is defined and model.batch is not none -%}
    {%- set bound = " AND col::DATE >= '" ~ model.batch.event_time_start ~ "'::DATE AND col::DATE < '" ~ model.batch.event_time_end ~ "'::DATE" -%}
{%- endif -%}
```

compiles under Fusion to an **always-empty half-open window** (`col >= '2025-01-01' AND col < '2025-01-01'`), silently dropping rows the unit test expects. The unit test fails with no code change — the model output differs purely because of how the engine populates `model.batch` during unit-test compilation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A microbatch model (`incremental_strategy='microbatch'`, `event_time=...`, `begin=...`) that reads a non-event-time source and applies a manual `model.batch`-derived date bound as above.
2. A unit test with `given` rows dated inside `begin..now`.
3. Run the unit test on dbt-core 1.11 → passes (bound not applied, `model.batch is None`).
4. Run the same unit test on Fusion 2.0.6 → fails; the bounded branches return 0 rows because `event_time_start == event_time_end`.

### Expected behavior

In the unit-test context, `model.batch` should be `None` under Fusion, matching dbt-core — so `model.batch`-guarded logic is skipped during unit tests.

### Actual behavior

`model.batch` is a non-None object with a zero-width window (`event_time_start == event_time_end`), causing manual batch bounds to filter out all rows.

### Workaround

Additionally guard on a non-degenerate window:

```jinja
{%- if model.batch is defined and model.batch is not none and model.batch.event_time_start != model.batch.event_time_end -%}
```

This is a no-op under dbt-core (short-circuits at `is not none`) and under real microbatch execution (`event_time_start < event_time_end`); it only neutralizes Fusion's unit-test placeholder.

issues.title: [v2 Bug] Seed `column_types` keys are matched case-sensitively against lower-cased column names
issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?
- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior
On adapters where v2 folds seed column names to lower case (Postgres, Redshift, DuckDB, Salesforce, LakeCompute), a `column_types` key that matches an upper-case CSV header is silently ignored. The column gets its inferred type instead, and no warning is emitted.

### Expected Behavior
The same result as dbt 1.x: with header `EVENT_DATE` and `column_types: {EVENT_DATE: date}`, the seed has a `date` column.

### Steps To Reproduce
DuckDB, binary built from `main` at `759dbee1f` (`dbt --version`: 2.0.5):

`dbt_project.yml`
```yaml
name: duck_probe
version: "1.0"
config-version: 2
profile: duck
seeds:
  duck_probe:
    raw_upper_types:
      +column_types:
        EVENT_DATE: date
```

`seeds/raw_upper_types.csv`
```
EVENT_ID,EVENT_DATE
1,2026-09-15
2,2026-09-16
```

`dbt seed --full-refresh`, then `information_schema.columns` shows `event_date VARCHAR`. With the key written `event_date: date` instead, the column is `DATE`. (`--full-refresh` matters when the table already exists: a plain `dbt seed` truncates and reloads it, so the column keeps its previous type.)

### Where it comes from
- `crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/register_seeds.rs:96`: `adapt_schema` renames the columns with the adapter's `InferColumnNameStrategy`, and the data is persisted under that schema.
- `crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/runnable/seed.rs:194`: the seed's agate table is read back from that file, so the macro sees `event_date`.
- The seed macros look the type up by exact name: `column_override.get(col_name, inferred_type)`.
- `check_and_warn_missing_column_types` (`seed.rs:28`) compares lower-cased names, so it finds nothing to warn about.

dbt 1.x keeps the CSV header as written, so upper-case keys match upper-case headers there.

### Proposed fix
Resolve the `column_types` keys against the agate column names case-insensitively before the materialization runs, so both `EVENT_DATE` and `event_date` work. I'm happy to open the PR.

### Environment
- OS: macOS 26 (arm64)
- dbt: v2 built from `main` at `759dbee1f` (`dbt --version`: 2.0.5), debug build

### Which database adapter are you using?
DuckDB (also reproduced on Athena with the adapter PRs from #16252)

issues.title: [v2 Bug] Relation cache is populated non-deterministically during execution

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: A defect: Fusion behaves incorrectly versus expected/reference behavior.

labels.name: area:adapters
labels.description: The adapter framework/layer connecting Fusion to warehouses (dbt-adapter* crates).

issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

dbt v2 fills the relation cache while models are running: a schema is listed the first time a model asks for a relation in it. This has two problems:

1. **The listing happens whenever the first model asks for it.** By then other models may already have changed the warehouse, so the state cached for a schema depends on when, during the run, the first lookup for that schema happened.
2. **Several models can ask at the same time and each one lists the schema.** The listing that arrives last overwrites the others, so the cached state also depends on which thread finished first.

Both make the result of a run depend on thread timing. The same `dbt run` on the same project can behave differently from one run to the next, and `dbt run` can give a different result for a model than `dbt run --select <model>`.

dbt 1.x fills the cache once, before running any model (`populate_adapter_cache`), so every model sees the same state.

**Example (ClickHouse, project below).** `target_tbl` is a table and `mv_model` is a materialized view that writes into it. In one commit the MV stops writing into `target_tbl` and `target_tbl` changes its schema. dbt-clickhouse reads `existing_relation.mvs_pointing_to_it` to decide whether it may rebuild the table. On v2 the answer depends on timing:

| dbt | Result of the same `dbt run`, repeated |
|---|---|
| 1.12.3 + dbt-clickhouse 1.10.1 | refused every time ("schemas out of sync") |
| v2 main `049fe759e` | rebuilt every time |
| v2 main + #16429 | rebuilt three times, refused once |

Notes on #16429:
- Without #16429 ClickHouse has no cache and `target_tbl` reads the catalog when it starts (always after the MV moved, problem 1).
- With #16429 the cache is filled at the start by the first models, so `target_tbl` usually sees the MV unless a second listing lands after the drop and overwrites it (problem 2).

`dbt run --select target_tbl` refuses on every version, because no other model runs before it. The dbt-clickhouse integration test `TestMVWithExplicitTargetForcesOnSchemaChangeFailInTable` is flaky on v2 for this reason.


### Expected Behavior

A schema should be:
- Listed once per invocation, with concurrent lookups waiting for that listing instead of repeating it
- Listed before the first model runs (dbt 1.x `populate_adapter_cache`, respecting `--cache-selected-only`). 

After that, the cache should only change through `cache_added` / `cache_dropped` / `cache_renamed`, which v2 already does.

### Steps To Reproduce

ClickHouse 26.3, single node, profile with `threads: 4`.

`seeds/people.csv`

```csv
id,name,department
1,Dade,engineering
2,Kate,engineering
3,Alfie,sales
```

`models/sources.yml`

```yaml
version: 2
sources:
  - name: raw
    schema: "{{ target.schema }}"
    tables:
      - name: people
```

`models/upstream_slow.sql` (any upstream model that takes a few seconds)

```sql
{{ config(materialized='table') }}
select number as id, sleepEachRow(0.2) as s from numbers(10)
```

`models/target_tbl.sql`

```sql
{{ config(materialized='table') }}
-- depends_on: {{ ref('upstream_slow') }}
select toInt32(0) as id, '' as name
{%- if var('extra_col', false) %}, toInt32(0) as extra_col{% endif %}
where 0
```

`models/mv_model.sql`

```sql
{{ config(materialized='materialized_view') }}
{%- if var('point_to_target', false) %}
{{ materialization_target_table(ref('target_tbl')) }}
{%- endif %}
select id, name from {{ source('raw', 'people') }} where department = 'engineering'
```

```shell
dbt seed
dbt run --vars '{point_to_target: true}'   # step 1: the MV writes into target_tbl
dbt run --vars '{extra_col: true}'         # step 2: target_tbl changes schema, the MV stops pointing at it
```

Repeat steps 1 and 2 a few times and compare the result of `target_tbl` in step 2. Then run step 2 as `dbt run --select target_tbl --vars '{extra_col: true}'`.

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6)
- CPU: ARM
- dbt distribution and version: `dbt-oss 2.0.5` built from main `049fe759e` (also tested with PR #16429, `561acda3b`). Comparison: dbt-core 1.12.3, dbt-adapters 1.24.5, dbt-clickhouse 1.10.1
- ClickHouse 26.3.12.3 (Docker, single node), adbc_clickhouse 0.1.1
```

### Which database adapter are you using?

clickhouse

### Is this a discrepancy vs. dbt 1.x?

- [x] Yes — this works in dbt 1.x but not in dbt v2.x

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: [v2 Bug] Redshift strict analysis drops user-defined _partitiondate after SELECT *
issues.body:
## Current Behavior

With dbt v2.0.6 and the Redshift adapter, `dbt compile --static-analysis strict` reports `dbt0227: No column _partitiondate found` in a downstream model, even though the referenced upstream model explicitly defines `_partitiondate` as a normal string-literal alias. The same upstream model's `_executiontime` alias is resolved successfully.

I reproduced this in a minimal two-model project without a live warehouse connection. In a larger Redshift project, the same diagnostic occurred in many staging models that select this synthetic column from their base models.

## Expected Behavior

Strict SQL analysis should preserve `_partitiondate` as an ordinary user-defined column across the upstream model and `SELECT *` expansion, just as it does `_executiontime`, and compile the downstream model successfully.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a minimal project with a Redshift profile (dummy connection values are sufficient; no warehouse connection is needed).
2. Add `models/base.sql`:

```sql
select
    1 as id,
    '20260925' as _partitiondate,
    current_timestamp as _executiontime
```

3. Add `models/repro.sql`:

```sql
with source as (
    select *
    from {{ ref('base') }}
)
select
    id,
    _partitiondate,
    _executiontime
from source
```

4. Run:

```sh
dbt compile --project-dir . --profiles-dir . --target dev --static-analysis strict --no-partial-parse
```

## Relevant log output

```text
[error] [UnresolvedIdentifier (dbt0227)]: No column _partitiondate found. Available are source._executiontime, source.id
  --> models/repro.sql:7:5
```

Setting `static_analysis='off'` on the downstream model avoids the diagnostic, but also disables analysis for that model.

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- CPU: ARM
- dbt distribution and version: dbt v2.0.6
- Adapter: Redshift (`redshift 0.21.0.dev+dbt0.18.8`)
- Mode: `--static-analysis strict`

## Additional Context

This may be related to the handling of BigQuery partition pseudo-columns, but this case is on Redshift and `_partitiondate` is an ordinary alias created by the model SQL, not a warehouse pseudo-column. Related reports: #13516 and #14383.

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

Indexing the result of `modules.re.search` or `modules.re.match` renders an empty string, for group numbers (`m[0]`, `m[1]`) and group names (`m['num']`) alike. No error is raised. `m.group(n)` returns the right value.

### Expected Behavior

The same as dbt 1.x, where `m[g]` is Python's `re.Match.__getitem__` and returns the same as `m.group(g)`: `m[0]` is the whole match, `m[1]` the first group, `m['num']` the named group.

### Steps To Reproduce

`dbt_project.yml`
```yaml
name: re_repro
version: "1.0"
profile: re_repro
model-paths: ["models"]
```

`profiles.yml`
```yaml
re_repro:
  target: dev
  outputs:
    dev:
      type: duckdb
      path: ":memory:"
```

`models/probe.sql`
```sql
{%- set m = modules.re.search('(?P<name>[a-z]+)-(?P<num>[0-9]+)', 'order-42') -%}
select
  '{{ m[0] }}'      as index_0,
  '{{ m[1] }}'      as index_1,
  '{{ m[2] }}'      as index_2,
  '{{ m["num"] }}'  as index_name,
  '{{ m.group(2) }}' as group_2

```

Run `dbt compile --select probe` and read `target/compiled/re_repro/models/probe.sql`.

### Relevant log output

dbt-core 1.12.5 with dbt-duckdb 1.11.0:
```sql
select
  'order-42'      as index_0,
  'order'      as index_1,
  '42'      as index_2,
  '42'  as index_name,
  '42' as group_2
```

dbt-oss 2.0.5, and `main` at 759dbee1f built from source:
```sql
select
  ''      as index_0,
  ''      as index_1,
  ''      as index_2,
  ''  as index_name,
  '42' as group_2
```

### Environment

- OS: macOS, arm64
- dbt v2: dbt-oss 2.0.5 from PyPI; `main` at 759dbee1f built from source
- dbt 1.x for comparison: dbt-core 1.12.5, dbt-duckdb 1.11.0

### Which database adapter are you using?

DuckDB for the reproduction. Found through the dbt-athena macro package (#16252).

### Is this a discrepancy vs. dbt 1.x?

- [x] Yes — this works in dbt 1.x but not in dbt v2.x

### Additional Context

`Capture::get_value` answers an integer key only for `re.findall` results (`is_findall`) and returns `None` for match and search results, which renders empty:
https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt/blob/759dbee1fc734dbc7aeddfe5bfa7bb0a47fa37f1/crates/dbt-jinja/minijinja-contrib/src/modules/re.rs#L943-L948

The restriction came with ad768967dac910cb6ba7432d569c6933850eb255 ("fix(re): make findall Capture sliceable as a sequence"), on the grounds that Python's `Match` object does not support index access. It does: `Match.__getitem__` accepts a group number or name (Python 3.6+). What `Match` does not support is slicing, iteration and `len()`, and those can stay as they are.

Suggested change: in `get_value`, for match and search results, return the group for an integer key and for a named-group key; leave `repr`, `enumerate` and slicing unchanged.

Impact: dbt-athena's `process_bucket_column.sql` reads `bucket_match[1]` and `bucket_match[2]`, so bucket-partitioned Iceberg tables fail with `undefined value` on dbt v2. Any project macro that indexes a match gets empty strings without an error.

With `--state` pointing at a manifest written by dbt 1.12, `state:modified.body` selects every unit test in the project, even when nothing has changed. Plain `state:modified` doesn't select them. Against a manifest written by v2, nothing is selected.

The docs say state comparison works across mixed v1 and v2 environments during a migration ([Upgrade versions in dbt platform](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/dbt-versions/upgrade-dbt-platform-version)). In practice, a CI job on v2 that defers to a v1 environment runs every unit test on every PR. On our project that was about 220 unit tests for a PR that touched no dbt files.


### Expected Behavior

An unchanged unit test isn't selected by `state:modified.body`, whichever version wrote the state manifest.


### Steps To Reproduce


`dbt_project.yml`:

```yaml
name: repro
version: "1.0.0"
profile: repro
```

`models/my_model.sql`:

```sql
select 1 as id
```

```yaml
unit_tests:
  - name: test_my_model

      rows:
        - {id: 1}
```

```sh
dbt parse --target-path target_v1

# dbt v2

# unit_test.repro.my_model.test_my_model
```
