_No response_

issues.title: [v2 Bug] BigQuery adapter hydrates the full relation cache via one REST call per object — turns every non-debug command into a multi-minute stall on a populated dataset

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: A defect: Fusion behaves incorrectly versus expected/reference behavior.

labels.name: adapter:bigquery
labels.description: Concerns the BigQuery adapter / SQL dialect.

labels.name: area:adapters
labels.description: The adapter framework/layer connecting Fusion to warehouses (dbt-adapter* crates).

issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

Every `dbt` subcommand that needs the relation cache — `compile`, `show`, `seed`, `run`, `build` — pays a fixed ~5-6 minute delay before doing any real warehouse work, on every single invocation, regardless of how many/few nodes are selected or how much data is involved. `dbt debug` (which skips relation-cache hydration) consistently completes in ~3 seconds.

**Root cause, confirmed via HTTP-level trace (`GODEBUG=http1debug=1,http2debug=1`) of a single-seed run:**

```
dbt seed -s single_seed_name --no-defer --target dev --log-level debug
```

- 18:28:34 — process starts; impersonated-credential token exchange (`sts.googleapis.com` → `iamcredentials.googleapis.com:generateAccessToken`)
- 18:28:35 to 18:34:03 (**5m28s**) — dbt walks the *entire* target dataset:
  - 47 paginated `GET .../datasets/shared_dev_dataset/tables?pageToken=...` calls to list every table (2,340 objects, confirmed independently via `bq ls`)
  - then **2,340 individual `GET .../tables/<name>?view=BASIC` calls — exactly one per object in the dataset**, sequential, not batched
  - plus 2 `GET .../datasets?all=true` calls enumerating all datasets in the project (22 total — a much smaller contributor, see #16297 above)
- 18:34:04 (**1 second** after the last enumeration call) — the actual seed load job is submitted (`POST /upload/.../jobs?uploadType=multipart`)
- Run completes ~18:34:11

So **2,340 of ~2,344 total BigQuery API calls (>99%) are per-object metadata GETs that happen before any query/load job is submitted**, for a `seed` operation on a single 247-row file. The actual work takes ~1 second; the wait is 100% relation-cache hydration.

Cross-checked against `dbt.log` across multiple independent runs (with and without OTEL env vars, single-seed and 6-seed batches) — the identical signature recurs every time: all nodes "start" instantly, one long silent gap, then all real work bursts through in seconds once the gap ends.


### Expected Behavior

`compile`/`seed`/`show`/`run`/`build` should take roughly as long as the actual query/load work requires (single-digit seconds for a trivial seed), matching dbt Core 1.x behavior — not pay a multi-minute tax that scales with how many objects already exist in the target schema.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Point a BigQuery `dev` target at a dataset containing a large number of existing tables/views (this project: 2,340 objects in a single dataset, `shared_dev_dataset` — the project enforces a single shared schema across all developers via a custom `generate_schema_name` macro, so the object count only grows over time).
2. Run `dbt debug --target dev` — completes in ~3s, connection test OK.
3. Run `dbt seed -s <any single small seed> --no-defer --target dev` — hangs silently for ~5-6 minutes before the seed load actually starts; completes within seconds once it does.
4. Optional: repeat with `GODEBUG=http1debug=1,http2debug=1` set and the command's stdout/stderr redirected to a file, then `grep -oE '/tables/[a-zA-Z0-9_]+\?' <file> | sort -u | wc -l` — count matches the dataset's total object count almost exactly.
5. Contrast with `dbt compile -s <same seed/model> --target dev` and `dbt show` — **both also take ~5-6 minutes in this environment**, unlike the `#16318` report where `compile` was unaffected. This discrepancy (`compile` slow here vs. fast there) is unexplained and worth a maintainer's attention — it may indicate this project hits the hydration path from more entry points than the `#16318` repro did, or a difference between dbt versions (`2.0.6` here vs. `2.0.0-preview.218` in that report).

### Relevant log output

```shell
HTTP trace path-only excerpt (auth headers/tokens redacted):

18:28:35  GET /bigquery/v2/projects/<project>/datasets/shared_dev_dataset/tables?alt=json&pageToken=&prettyPrint=false
18:28:35  GET /bigquery/v2/projects/<project>/datasets/shared_dev_dataset/tables?alt=json&pageToken=user1_table_a&prettyPrint=false
... (47 paginated list calls total) ...
18:28:3x  GET /bigquery/v2/projects/<project>/datasets/shared_dev_dataset/tables/user2_table_b?alt=json&prettyPrint=false&view=BASIC
18:28:3x  GET /bigquery/v2/projects/<project>/datasets/shared_dev_dataset/tables/user3_table_c?alt=json&prettyPrint=false&view=BASIC
... (2,340 individual per-object GET calls total, one per table/view in the dataset) ...
18:34:03  GET /bigquery/v2/projects/<project>/datasets/shared_dev_dataset/tables/user4_table_d?alt=json&prettyPrint=false&view=BASIC   <- last enumeration call
18:34:04  POST /upload/bigquery/v2/projects/<project>/jobs?alt=json&prettyPrint=false&uploadType=multipart   <- actual seed load, 1s later


`dbt.log` timing signature (from an earlier 6-seed batch run, consistent across every run observed this investigation):

Started running (6 nodes) at 16:30:17.426
... silence ...
Applying DROP at 16:35:52.691   (~5m35s gap)
... all 6 seeds' real work (drop/create/load) complete within the next ~20s ...


`dbt debug` vs single-seed timing (this session):

dbt debug --target dev                                       -> 3.1s, "All checks passed!"
dbt seed -s single_seed_name --no-defer --target dev  -> 4m28s (traced run: 5m37s)


**Side-by-side confirmation against dbt Core 1.12 (same machine, same `dev` target, same credentials, same populated dataset)**:

dbt-core==1.12.0 / dbt-bigquery==1.12.0
1 of 1 START seed file shared_dev_dataset.user5_seed_table ... [RUN]
1 of 1 OK loaded seed file ... [INSERT 247 in 5.86s]
Finished running 1 seed in 0 hours 0 minutes and 8.41 seconds (8.41s)

Identical seed, identical dataset, identical impersonated-identity credentials: **8.41s on 1.x vs. ~5-6 minutes on 2.0/Fusion.**
```

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200, x86_64
- dbt distribution and version: `dbt 2.0.6` (Fusion)
- CPU: 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1145G7 @ 2.60GHz (2.61 GHz)
- Comparison baseline: `dbt-core 1.12.0` / `dbt-bigquery 1.12.0`, same machine
- Target dataset: 2,340 tables/views (single shared dev schema, `shared_dev_dataset`)
- Project: 22 datasets total
```

### Which database adapter are you using?

bigquery

### Is this a discrepancy vs. dbt 1.x?

- [x] Yes — this works in dbt 1.x but not in dbt v2.x

### Additional Context

**Leading hypothesis:** relation-cache hydration in the BigQuery ADBC driver enumerates every object in the target dataset via one REST call per object (`GetObjects`-style, matching the mechanism described in #16318) rather than a single batched/filtered call, so wall-clock cost scales linearly with dataset population (here: exactly 2,340 calls for 2,340 objects). `dbt debug` is fast because it's the only command that doesn't hydrate this cache.

**Likely code location (not independently verified against source):** the observed call shape — paginated `tables.list` followed by one `tables.get?view=BASIC` per object — matches how the Arrow ADBC `GetObjects` metadata call would have to be implemented against the BigQuery REST API if it needs per-table detail that `tables.list` doesn't return (e.g. schema/column info): the driver would have no batched endpoint to fall back to and would loop `tables.get` once per object. If so, the fix likely belongs in the Go `adbc-driver-bigquery` implementation (now under `adbc-drivers/bigquery`, previously `apache/arrow-adbc`) rather than in dbt-core/Fusion itself — flagging so maintainers can route this to the right repo, though I have not read that driver's source to confirm.

**Investigated and ruled out / not applicable:**
- *WIF/service-account-impersonation OAuth scope bugs* (`arrow-adbc#3522`/`#3174`/`#3523`) — these are about `403` errors reading Drive-backed external tables, not delays. The impersonation flow itself completes fine here (see token-exchange timestamps in the trace above); it's not the bottleneck.
- *Total datasets in the project* (#16297's mechanism) — only 22 datasets in this project; per the reporter's own formula this would cost well under a second, not minutes. The per-object table enumeration within the single populated dataset is the dominant cost by roughly two orders of magnitude (2,340 calls vs. 2 project-level `datasets?all=true` calls).
- *OpenTelemetry (OTEL) exporter env vars* — separately investigated and confirmed unrelated. Persistent `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` user env vars pointing at an unreachable collector cause a much worse, independent hang (25+ minutes, no startup banner at all), but disabling OTEL entirely (`OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true`) does **not** change the ~5-6 minute baseline delay described in this issue — confirmed via a controlled A/B test. Flagging so maintainers don't need to re-chase that path.
- *Permission gaps on the impersonated identity* — checked via `bq show` on the dataset ACL: the impersonated service account has an explicit, dataset-level `READER` role (not a partial/legacy per-table grant), so uneven access isn't causing extra retries.

**Open question for maintainers:** in the `#16318` repro, `dbt compile` was unaffected (0 jobs, ~8s) while `build`/`run` were slow. In this environment, `dbt compile` and `dbt show` are *also* affected (~5-6 min, per direct observation this session) alongside `seed`/`run`/`build`. If `compile` isn't supposed to trigger relation-cache hydration, that divergence may be worth a separate look — possibly version-related (`2.0.6` vs. the `2.0.0-preview.218` in #16318).

One candidate explanation raised during review: projects that use macros like `dbt_utils.star()`, `adapter.get_columns_in_relation()`, or `adapter.get_relation()` inside models (or `on-run-start`/`on-run-end` hooks) force relation resolution at parse time, which would make `compile` pay the same hydration cost as `build`/`run`. I checked this specifically — this project has no `on-run-start`/`on-run-end` hooks, and the only matches for those macro patterns are in a handful of one-off macros invoked via `dbt run-operation` (prod-vs-dev drift-checking scripts), not inside the regular model DAG that `compile`/`seed` walk. So that explanation doesn't fit this repro as-is, but it's worth maintainers ruling in/out for other reporters, or checking whether Fusion's own static analysis resolves relations during parsing regardless of explicit macro usage.

**Suggested fix direction (matching #16318's implied ask):** batch relation-cache hydration into a single filtered/paginated metadata call (e.g. a `SELECT` against `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, or the BigQuery `tables.list` response's existing per-item fields) instead of one `tables.get` REST call per object, so cost stops scaling linearly with dataset population.

issues.title: [v2 Bug] dbt format silently no-ops on deeply nested SQL exceeding parse depth 255 (symbolic mode); max_parse_depth config is ignored
issues.body:
## Summary
`dbt format` behaves inconsistently across its formatting modes when run against SQL that exceeds the parser's max nesting depth (255). The default mode (`symbolic`) reports success and silently makes no changes, masking a real parse failure that only `rendered` mode surfaces. The limit is specific to the dbt v2 parser and is not configurable, despite `.sqlfluff` exposing a `max_parse_depth` key.

## Environment
- dbt 2.0.6 (v2 engine)
- Adapter: Databricks
- OS: macOS

## Behavior by mode

| Mode | Result |
|---|---|
| `symbolic` (default) | Reports "Finished 'format' successfully". **No changes made.** Silent no-op. |
| `rendered` | Fails with the real error (see below). |
| `turbo` | Runs, but only applies superficial re-indentation — does not reflow the broken layout. |

## Exact error (rendered mode)
```
[error] [SyntaxInvalid (dbt0101)]: Failed to parse SQL for format: parse error: "Maximum parse depth exceeded (limit 255). This may indicate deeply nested SQL or a malicious input." pos: Some(1789)
```

## Root cause
Cumulative parse-tree depth across the entire model statement — not any single construct, and not raw file size.

Verified via bisection: a `config()` block, a chain of ~19 `LEFT JOIN`s, an internal macro producing ~17 `UNION DISTINCT`-chained CTEs, and a wide `SELECT` with nested `CASE`/`GREATEST`/`LEAST`/`COALESCE` + `MD5(TO_JSON(STRUCT(...)))` — each passes `dbt format` cleanly in isolation. Combined, they fail, and the failure position scales with statement size:

| Macro CTE count | Result | Error `pos` |
|---|---|---|
| 17 | fails | 1789 |
| 8 | fails | 1033 |
| 3 (with full join/SELECT) | fails | 587 |
| 3 (minimal SELECT, no joins) | passes | — |

The shifting `pos` indicates a running parse-depth counter hitting a hardcoded ceiling (255), not a fixed byte offset.

Likely mechanism: the v2 parser builds one parse tree per statement. Depth accumulates through the outer wrapper → CTE → a wide `SELECT` with several levels of nested `CASE`/`GREATEST`/`LEAST`/`COALESCE` expressions → ~19 chained `LEFT JOIN`s → `UNION`-chained CTEs (each `UNION` adds a nesting level) wrapped in an aggregate-over-subquery. No individual branch reaches 255, but the combined statement does. Other large models in our project format fine because they don't stack this many nesting dimensions in a single statement — confirming this is about nesting depth, not file size.

## Comparison with classic SQLFluff / v1 engine
Classic SQLFluff (used by dbt Studio IDE's Lint-and-Fix, which runs the v1 engine per the [docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/platform/studio-ide/lint-format)) does not hit this limit on the same model — Lint-and-Fix completes cleanly with no depth error. This confirms the 255 parse-depth ceiling is specific to the v2 parser (`dbt format`/`dbt lint` on the v2 CLI), not an inherent limitation of the underlying SQL structure.

## `max_parse_depth` is not honored
`.sqlfluff` supports a `max_parse_depth` key that (per community reports) worked in an earlier preview build to raise this limit. In dbt 2.0.6, it is silently ignored:
- Setting `max_parse_depth = 1000` produces an identical failure, still reporting "(limit 255)."
- Setting `max_parse_depth = 5` against an unrelated, normally-clean model does not fail it — confirming the key isn't read at all (not just clamped).

All other `.sqlfluff` settings (dialect, capitalization rules, exclude_rules, etc.) are correctly honored, so this isn't a general config-loading problem — `max_parse_depth` specifically appears unimplemented or dropped in the current v2 release.

## Expected vs actual
- **Expected:** `dbt format` either succeeds with real formatting applied, or fails loudly in every mode when it can't parse the input. If a project sets `max_parse_depth`, that setting should be honored.
- **Actual:** `symbolic` mode exits 0 and claims success while doing nothing; only `rendered` mode reveals the underlying `dbt0101` parse-depth failure. `max_parse_depth` in `.sqlfluff` has no effect.

## Minimal repro (synthetic — not our production model)
This is not our production model. It's a generated worst case that reproduces the same failure class: enough nested structure to exceed parse depth 255. Adjust `N` up/down to find your engine's actual threshold.

```sql
-- generate_repro.sql — deeply nested boolean expression to exceed parse depth
-- generated programmatically, e.g.:
-- python3 -c "
-- n = 140
-- expr = 'col_0'
-- for i in range(1, n):
--     expr = f'({expr} + col_{i})'
-- print(f'select {expr} as deep_expr from source_table')
-- "

with base as (
    select * from {{ ref('source_table') }}
),

deeply_nested as (
    select
        ((((((((((((((((((((col_0 + col_1) + col_2) + col_3) + col_4) + col_5)
        + col_6) + col_7) + col_8) + col_9) + col_10) + col_11) + col_12)
        + col_13) + col_14) + col_15) + col_16) + col_17) + col_18) + col_19)
        -- ... continue nesting until parse depth 255 is exceeded
        as deep_expr
    from base
)

select * from deeply_nested
```

Note: in our real-world trigger, the nesting came from ~19 chained `LEFT JOIN`s combined with `{% if is_incremental() %}` conditional logic and a macro-generated `UNION`-chained CTE stack in a single model — size alone isn't the trigger (other large models format fine); it's specifically parse-tree depth.

## Current workarounds
- `--jinja-render-mode turbo` — survives the limit (different, more tolerant parse path), but only does superficial re-indentation.
- Format via dbt Studio IDE's Lint-and-Fix, which uses the v1 engine.

## Ask
Either raise the v2 parser's hardcoded 255 parse-depth limit, or restore/implement support for `max_parse_depth` in `.sqlfluff` so it can be configured per-project.

## Related issues (not duplicates)
- #15553 — v2 lint/format silently processing the whole project when given multi-file args. Related silent-behavior theme, different root cause.
- #12329 — old Python `sqlparse` grouping-depth limit in dbt Core (pre-v2). **Not the same issue** — this is the v2 parser under dbt 2.0, with a different limit (255) and a different silent-failure mode (symbolic no-op vs. an explicit error in Core).
- #16391 — related community request (SELECT * ban lint rule), same #dbt-fusion-engine thread context, unrelated bug.

## Impact
The `symbolic` default mode's silent success is the most concerning part: CI/local runs can report a clean `dbt format` while doing nothing, giving false confidence that formatting standards are being enforced. The non-functional `max_parse_depth` setting removes the one documented escape hatch.

issues.title: [v2 Bug] Static analysis: Redshift `HLL_CREATE_SKETCH` not recognized as an aggregate → false `UnaggregatedColumn (dbt0213)`

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: A defect: Fusion behaves incorrectly versus expected/reference behavior.

labels.name: area:adapters
labels.description: The adapter framework/layer connecting Fusion to warehouses (dbt-adapter* crates).

issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

Under `--static-analysis strict`, a model that uses Amazon Redshift's HyperLogLog aggregate
`HLL_CREATE_SKETCH(<col>)` in a `GROUP BY` query fails with:
 
```
[error] [UnaggregatedColumn (dbt0213)]: Un-aggregated columns in aggregation context:
s.visitor_id must be aggregated or appear in a GROUP BY clause
```
 
`HLL_CREATE_SKETCH` **is** an aggregate function in Redshift (it returns one `HLLSKETCH` per group and
ignores NULLs — AWS docs below), so its argument does **not** need to appear in `GROUP BY`. Fusion's
static analyzer does not recognize `HLL_CREATE_SKETCH` as an aggregate and therefore treats the
argument column as un-aggregated. The SQL compiles and runs correctly in dbt Core and directly in
Redshift.
 
This is the aggregate-recognition analogue of #15299 (there the analyzer mishandles types in a GROUP BY
context; here it mishandles which functions aggregate).
 

### Expected Behavior

`HLL_CREATE_SKETCH(col)` (and the related Redshift HLL aggregates) should be recognized as aggregate
functions, so their arguments are not required in `GROUP BY` and no `dbt0213` is raised. No exemption
should be necessary.

### Steps To Reproduce

Reproduces only when Fusion can probe a real Redshift table schema (source or materialized ref).
 
1. An upstream table `sessions` with columns `visit_date`, `visitor_id`:
 
   ```sql
   -- models/sessions.sql  (materialized as table so its schema exists in the warehouse)
   select '2024-05-01'::date as visit_date, 1 as visitor_id
   ```
 
2. A downstream model that builds an HLL sketch per day:
 
   ```sql
   -- models/sessions_daily.sql
   select
       visit_date,
       hll_create_sketch(visitor_id) as unique_visitors_sketch
   from {{ ref('sessions') }}
   group by visit_date
   ```
 
3. Compile with strict static analysis:
 
   ```
   dbt compile --static-analysis strict --select sessions_daily
   ```

- Replacing `hll_create_sketch(visitor_id)` with a recognized aggregate, e.g. `count(distinct visitor_id)`,
  compiles clean — confirming the issue is aggregate recognition, not the GROUP BY itself.
- The model runs successfully in Redshift and under dbt Core (which does not statically analyze).
- Wrapping the argument in a recognized aggregate (`hll_create_sketch(max(visitor_id))`) clears the error

issues.title: [v2 Bug] local unit tests: `REGEXP_REPLACE` replaces only the first match (BigQuery replaces all)
issues.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

Local unit tests (`compute: local`, behind `DBT_ENGINE_EXPERIMENTAL_LOCAL_UNIT_TESTS=true`) are
v2-only, so there is no 1.x behavior to compare against.

### Current Behavior

On BigQuery, `REGEXP_REPLACE` replaces every match. In a local unit test only the first match is
replaced:

```
│ raw_text   ┆ digits                │
│ 10,000,000 ┆ 10000000 -> 10000,000 │
```

Control on BigQuery: `select regexp_replace('10,000,000', r'[^0-9]', '')` returns `'10000000'`.

Like the `LEAST` case, this does not error; the value is just different. A common pattern such as
`safe_cast(regexp_replace(amount, r'[^0-9]', '') as int64)` becomes `NULL` locally for any value with
more than one separator. We also see it in the `ga4` package's own unit test
(`query_parameter_removal` in Velir/dbt-ga4), which passes on BigQuery and fails locally because the
second query parameter is left in place. (DuckDB's `regexp_replace` replaces the first match unless
the `'g'` option is given, which may be related; not confirmed.)

### Expected Behavior

`REGEXP_REPLACE` should replace all matches in local unit tests, matching BigQuery.

### Steps To Reproduce

```sql
-- models/src.sql
select 'x' as raw_text, 1 as n
```
```sql
-- models/regexp_replace_model.sql
select raw_text, regexp_replace(raw_text, r'[^0-9]', '') as digits
from {{ ref('src') }}
```
```yaml
unit_tests:
  - name: regexp_replace_all_matches_local
    model: regexp_replace_model
    config:
      compute: local
    given:
      - input: ref('src')
        format: sql
        rows: |
          select '10,000,000' as raw_text, 1 as n
    expect:
      rows:
        - { raw_text: '10,000,000', digits: '10000000' }
```

### Environment

- dbt: 2.0.4 and 2.0.6 (same result)

pull_requests.title: Respect indirect_selection set in dbt_project.yml flags
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16496

### Problem

`indirect_selection` set under `flags:` in `dbt_project.yml` is ignored. The mode is only taken from `--indirect-selection` / `DBT_INDIRECT_SELECTION`, so a project configured like this:

```yaml
flags:
  indirect_selection: cautious
```

Still selects tests with eager. For example, `dbt build --select model_a` runs tests that also depend on unselected models. In dbt 1.x, the project flag sets the default mode.

### Solution

Read flags.indirect_selection from `dbt_project.yml` in `dbt-clap-core`.

It then applies that mode to --select / --exclude and EvalArgs.indirect_selection, exactly as the env var is applied today. Every downstream consumer (selector resolution, both partial-parse paths, telemetry invocation args) picks it up unchanged.

- `FlagsBlock.indirect_selection` is an `Option<String>` and is parsed case-insensitively afterwards. A typed enum field would make an invalid value fail deserialization of the whole block, and that would silently drop the other early-read flags. 
- Unit tests cover:
  - reading the flag, including case-insensitive values
  - missing and invalid values
  - the other flags still being read when this value is invalid
  - falling back to the project flag
  - the CLI overriding the project flag

### Checklist

- [x] I have read [the contributing guide](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and understand what's expected of me.
- [x] I have run this code in development, and it appears to resolve the stated issue.

pull_requests.title: fix: keep a package's other macros when a unit test overrides one (#16477)
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16477

### Problem

When a unit test overrides a package-qualified macro in `overrides.macros`, such as `my_project.is_ci`, every other macro in that package becomes undefined, and the test fails with `value of type undefined is not callable`. dbt-core replaces only the overridden macro.

`bind_override_macros` in `crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/renderable/renderable/unit_test.rs` puts a one-entry map with the stub in front of the package namespace, using `ObjectOverlay`. As the issue explains, that map answers every other name with undefined. The overlay also never asks the package namespace, which resolves macros only through `get_property`.

Reproduced on DuckDB with the macros and model from the issue (`pick_label()` calls `my_project.is_ci()`), both in the root project and with the project installed as a package through `local: ..`:

| Unit test | dbt 2.0.6 / 2.0.7 | dbt-core 1.12.5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| overrides `my_project.is_ci: true`, expects `ci` | error | pass |
| overrides `my_project.unused_macro: "stub"`, expects `local` | error | pass |
| no override, expects `local` | pass | pass |

### Solution

- `ObjectOverlay` skips undefined values, as the issue suggests, so the stub no longer answers names it does not define.
- It also forwards `get_property` to its layers in order. Package namespaces resolve their macros there, not in `get_value`, so skipping undefined values alone still fails, with `unknown method: map has no method named pick_label`.
- Macros called through the package still see the override: `pick_label()` gets the stubbed `is_ci` and returns `ci`, as in dbt-core.

Tested with `cargo nextest run -p dbt-tasks-sa` (new tests: `test_package_macro_override_is_seen_by_other_package_macros`, `test_package_macro_override_keeps_unrelated_package_macros`). The tests use a small namespace that, like `DbtNamespace`, resolves macros only through `get_property`, since `DbtNamespace` is not reachable from `dbt-tasks-sa` without adding a dependency. With a local build, all three unit tests pass in both setups.

This does not change the error location the issue also reports.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read [the contributing guide](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and understand what's expected of me.
- [x] I have run this code in development, and it appears to resolve the stated issue.

pull_requests.title: fix: return the group when indexing a modules.re match object (#16451)
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16451

### Problem

Indexing a match object from `modules.re.search` or `modules.re.match` (`m[0]`, `m[1]`, `m['name']`) renders an empty string without an error, while `m.group(1)` works. In dbt-core, `m[g]` is Python's `re.Match.__getitem__` and returns the same as `m.group(g)`.

`Capture::get_value` in `crates/dbt-jinja/minijinja-contrib/src/modules/re.rs` answered integer keys only for `re.findall` results and had no lookup by group name.

Reproduced on DuckDB with the project from the issue (`dbt compile`):

| Expression | dbt 2.0.6 / 2.0.7 | dbt-core 1.12.5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `m[0]`, `m[1]`, `m[2]`, `m["num"]` | empty | `order-42`, `order`, `42`, `42` |
| `m.group(2)` | `42` | `42` |

### Solution

- As suggested in the issue, integer keys now index the groups for match and search results too (`m[0]` is the whole match). `re.findall` results work as before.
- String keys check the attribute names first (`pos`, `string`, ...) and then the named groups, so `m.pos` keeps working. One difference from dbt-core remains: a group named like one of those attributes, such as `(?P<pos>...)`, read as `m['pos']` returns the attribute, because item and attribute access share one lookup here.
- Slicing, iteration and `len()` stay unsupported, as in Python.

Tested with `cargo nextest run -p minijinja-contrib` (new tests: `test_re_match_capture_index_access_returns_group`, `test_re_match_result_index_access_returns_group`, `test_re_match_capture_missing_group_is_undefined`, `test_re_match_capture_attributes_still_resolve`). With a local build, the project from the issue renders `order-42`, `order`, `42`, `42`, and these cases also match dbt-core: `re.match` results, missing groups (`m[5]`, `m['nope']` and `m[-1]` render empty), and `m.pos`, `m.string` and `m.lastgroup`.

### Checklist

- [x] I have run this code in development, and it appears to resolve the stated issue.

pull_requests.title: fix: read column schemas of Snowflake stream sources
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

On Snowflake, Fusion fetches a source's columns with `describe table`. For a source that is a **stream**, Snowflake rejects that:

```
002030 (42601): SQL compilation error:
Invalid object type: 'TABLE'
```

The schema download fails (`dbt1014 Failed to download source schema`), and static analysis is turned off for every model downstream of the stream. They lose column lineage.

This PR retries on that exact error with:

```sql
select * from <relation> limit 0;
describe result '<query id of that select>';
```

- Both run on the same connection.
- `describe result` returns the same columns as `describe table` (`name`, `type`, `null?`, `comment`, ...), so `build_schema_from_desc_table` reads it unchanged.
- The select is described by its own query id rather than `last_query_id()`. A proxy or middleware may run statements on the session in between, and then `last_query_id()` returns the wrong schema.
- Neither statement advances the stream offset.

Other relations are unaffected: tables, views and missing relations never reach the fallback. If a fallback query fails, the original error is returned (a cancellation is still reported as a cancellation).

## Test plan

- Unit test: the error check matches the stream error, and does not match `Invalid object type: 'VIEW'` or "does not exist or not authorized".
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p dbt-adapter --all-targets` pass clean.
- Live test against a real Snowflake stream (throwaway test, not included). It calls `list_relations_schemas` through `AdbcEngine`, with debug assertions on:
  - `main`: the stream fails with the error above.
  - This branch: the stream returns `EVENTS` plus `METADATA$ACTION`, `METADATA$ISUPDATE`, `METADATA$ROW_ID`. The base table (control) is unchanged.

`snowflake__get_columns_in_relation` (`dbt-snowflake/macros/adapters.sql`) also uses `describe table`, so `adapter.get_columns_in_relation` on a stream likely fails the same way.

pull_requests.title: fix: keep project vars in unit tests with overrides.vars, and let has_var() see --vars (#16448)
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16448

### Problem

When a unit test sets `overrides.vars`, every other `var()` call in the model fails with `Required var '...' not found`. `apply_unit_test_overrides` in `crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/renderable/renderable/unit_test.rs` replaced the `var` function with one built from the CLI vars and the overrides only, so project and package vars were no longer visible.

While fixing this I found a related gap: `var.has_var()` returns `False` for vars passed with `--vars` and for unit test overrides, while `var()` returns them. `ConfiguredVar::contains_var` in `crates/dbt-jinja-vars/src/configured_var.rs` only checks project and package vars. Once unit tests use the same `var` as models, they would inherit this, so the fix is included here.

Reproduced on DuckDB:

| Case | dbt 2.0.6 / 2.0.7 | dbt-core 1.12.5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit test with `overrides.vars` whose model reads a project var | `Required var 'max_ts' not found` | pass |
| `var.has_var()` on a var passed with `--vars` | `False` | `True` |
| `var.has_var()` on a var set in `overrides.vars`, inside a unit test | `False` | `True` |

### Solution

- `ConfiguredVar::with_overrides` returns a copy of the package-aware `var` with the overrides added to the CLI vars, so they take precedence over CLI and project vars, as in dbt-core. `apply_unit_test_overrides` uses it when the environment's `var` is a `ConfiguredVar`, and keeps the previous behavior otherwise.
- `ConfiguredVar::contains_var` now checks the CLI vars, which include unit test overrides, before the project and package vars, like `var()` does.
- `ConfiguredVar` is re-exported from `dbt-jinja-utils` next to `Var`.

Tested with `cargo nextest run -p dbt-jinja-vars -p dbt-jinja-utils -p dbt-tasks-sa` (new tests: `overrides_take_precedence_and_keep_project_vars` and `has_var_sees_cli_vars_overrides_and_project_vars`). With a local build, the three cases above match dbt-core, and so do two more unit test cases: a `--vars` value stays visible when an unrelated var is overridden, and an override beats a `--vars` value.

## Summary
- The nightly release workflow (`Nightly Test Release to GitHub and PyPI`) has been failing every run at `validate-package-available-pypi`, always with "Manual intervention required" (e.g. runs 35204535784 through 36232307332).

pull_requests.title: fix: report mismatches for TIMESTAMP/DATETIME columns in unit test results (#15894)
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #15894

### Problem

Unit tests whose `expect` rows carry a wrong TIMESTAMP or DATETIME value pass.

`value_as_string` in `crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/materialize.rs` has dedicated arms for a handful of Arrow types (ints, floats, strings, booleans, `Decimal128`, `Timestamp(Second)`, `Timestamp(Nanosecond)`, `Date32`) and renders everything else as the literal `"[unsupported]"`. Warehouse TIMESTAMP and DATETIME columns arrive as `Timestamp(Microsecond, _)` (DuckDB, BigQuery), so the actual and the expected cell both render as `[unsupported]` and `compare_record_batches` reports a match.

Reproduced on dbt 2.0.5 and 2.0.6 with DuckDB (repro in the issue): a test expecting `ts: "2024-01-01 00:00:01"` against a model returning `00:00:00` passes, and the diff table of a failing control test shows `[unsupported]` in both timestamp columns. dbt-core 1.12.5 with dbt-duckdb reports all three mismatches in the same project.

### Solution

- Types without a dedicated arm now go through Arrow's display formatter (`ArrayFormatter`), which other crates in the workspace already use to render cells, so every value is rendered from its content.
- A type the formatter cannot render is an `ArrowError` out of `compare_record_batches` instead of a silent match: `value_as_string` returns `Result` and the comparison closure propagates it. Nulls keep rendering as `NULL`, matching the existing arms.
- The existing arms are untouched, so diff output for the types handled today does not change.

Tests (`cargo nextest run -p dbt-tasks-sa compare_record_batches_tests`): a mismatch is detected for microsecond timestamps with and without a timezone and for millisecond timestamps; equal microsecond values report no differences; the second-precision control is kept. The two microsecond tests fail on `main` without the fix.

Verified end to end with a local build against the DuckDB project from the issue: the wrong-value tests now fail with readable diffs (`2024-01-01T00:00:01 -> 2024-01-01T00:00:00`) and the all-correct control passes.

Note: because these columns are now compared, one pre-existing issue becomes visible. On DuckDB in a non-UTC session, a `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` fixture value is cast as `timestamp without time zone` (the timezone is dropped in `sql_types.rs`), so a correct `+00` expectation is re-interpreted in the session timezone and fails. Filed separately as #16470; this PR does not change fixture typing.

Alternative considered: explicit `Millisecond` and `Microsecond` arms in the style of the existing ones. The generic fallback covers those and every other type (`Date64`, `Time64`, other decimal widths, lists, structs) with less code.

pull_requests.title: Allow Mashumaro 3.22 with dbt-common 1.38
pull_requests.body:
Related to #12876.

### Problem

407f6caa1 capped Mashumaro below 3.15 after that release broke Core. 600fbe10b corrected NodeVersion and external partition union handling and raised the ceiling to <3.18. The remaining cap still excludes Mashumaro 3.20, which #12876 proposes to allow, and 3.22.

### Solution

Require dbt-common 1.38 for its Boolean passthrough fix [1] [2]. Mashumaro 3.15 began using Python truth testing for Boolean inputs [3]. Preserving their original types lets JSON Schema reject strings such as "false" instead of accepting them as true.

Raise the ceiling to <3.23. Mashumaro 3.22 retains the exact-type serialization strategy lookup used by that fix [4] and supports Core's Python 3.10 floor [5]. Keep the next minor release outside the range, following Core's policy for deeply used dependencies.

Core CI installs dbt-adapters from main [7]. A CI run using the adapter relaxation [6] must confirm that Mashumaro 3.22 is selected before it can qualify the widened range. Released installations also need an adapter release containing that change.

Prepared by Codex on behalf of Tamir Duberstein.

pull_requests.title: fix(selector): decide version:none from the parsed version
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16466

### Problem

`match_version` decided the `version:none` selector by probing the model's file stem for a `_v1` or `_v2` suffix, while the other three arms of the same function read the parsed version, and dbt-core's `VersionSelectorMethod` reads `node.version is None`.

A Fusion version is the raw YAML value stringified, so `collect_model_version_info` in `crates/dbt-parser/src/resolve/resolve_properties.rs` produces any of `3`, `10`, `1.0` or a non-numeric string, and `defined_in:` can place a version in a file with any name. The model field is `Option<StringOrInteger>`, so a numeric suffix probe cannot recover a string version. The suffix test misclassifies every model outside `_v1` and `_v2`, and produces a false positive in the other direction too: dbt only makes `orders_v1` a version when `versions:` declares it, so an unversioned model that merely ends in `_v1` is excluded from `version:none`.

| project state | correct | before |
|---|---|---|
| `versions: [v:1, v:2, v:3]`, file `orders_v3.sql` | no match | matched |
| `v: 1.0`, file `orders_v1.0.sql` | no match | matched |
| `versions: [v:1]` with `defined_in: orders_hist.sql` | no match | matched |
| unversioned model named `orders_v1` | matched | did not match |

The probe also ran two `expect()` calls on every `match_version` call, including for models whose `original_file_path` has no file name.

### Solution

Drop the probe and read the parsed version, which is what the other three arms already do:

```rust
"none" => Ok(node.version().is_none()),
```

That also removes the two `expect()` calls. `Path` stays imported and used elsewhere in the file, so the import set is unchanged.

Alternatives considered: deriving the zero value from `git rev-parse --show-object-format`-style probing has no analogue here, and keeping the suffix check as a fast path would still need the parsed value as the authority, so there is nothing to keep. Making `none` a fourth alias of the existing arms would change the selector's documented meaning, so I left it as a separate arm.

<details>
<summary>Testing plan</summary>

`main` at `7e4e937c4eef07e3837960507dea46c15c1db42b`, Rust 1.98.0, aarch64-apple-darwin. No database, network or credentials; the test constructs `DbtModel` literals through the existing `create_test_node` helper.

Before the fix, with only the new test added:

```
running 2 tests
test node_selector::tests::test_match_version ... ok
test node_selector::tests::test_match_version_none_uses_parsed_version_not_file_name ... FAILED

thread '...' panicked at crates/dbt-scheduler/src/node_selector.rs:1692:9:
a versioned model must never match version:none

test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 124 filtered out
```

With the fix, the whole crate:

```
$ cargo test -p dbt-scheduler
test result: ok. 126 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.01s
```

The pre-existing `test_match_version` is unchanged and still passes. It did not catch this because its `models/test_v1.sql` case sets `version = Some("1")` at the same time, so the two readings of "unversioned" happen to agree there.

Gates: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean. `cargo clippy -p dbt-scheduler --all-targets` reports nothing for `node_selector.rs`; `--workspace -D warnings` is already red on `main` in `dbt-adbc` and `dbt-tracing`, which this change does not touch. Per `AGENTS.md` I ran targeted `-p` commands rather than a blanket build.

A changelog entry is included as `.changes/unreleased/Fixes-20260926-024100.yaml`.

</details>

pull_requests.title: fix(seed): match column_types keys to seed column names case-insensitively
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16459

### Problem

On adapters that lower-case seed column names (Postgres, Redshift, DuckDB, Salesforce, LakeCompute), a `column_types` key written like an upper-case CSV header is ignored. With header `EVENT_DATE` and `column_types: {EVENT_DATE: date}`, the column is loaded as `VARCHAR` on DuckDB, with no warning. dbt 1.x gives `DATE`.

The columns reach the materialization already renamed by `adapt_schema` (`register_seeds.rs:96`), and the seed macros look the type up by exact name (`column_override.get(col_name, inferred_type)`).

### Solution

`execute_seed_remote` now aligns the `column_types` keys with the agate column names before calling `materialize_seed`. A key is renamed to a column's name only when:

- no column has exactly that name,
- exactly one column matches it case-insensitively,
- and the map has no key already spelled like that column.

Otherwise the key is left as it is, so exact keys keep their current behavior and ambiguous cases are not guessed. The seed node is cloned only when a key actually changes. The macros read `model['config'].column_types`, which comes from `deprecated_config`. `__seed_attr__.column_types` is aligned as well, so the two copies of the map stay identical for the rest of the task.

I kept the change in the seed task rather than in the macros, so the adapter macro packages stay identical to dbt 1.x.

### Verification

- Five unit tests on `align_column_types_keys`: case-only rename, exact key untouched, unknown key untouched, no rename when two columns match, exact key kept when both spellings are given.
- `cargo nextest run -p dbt-tasks-sa`: 190 passed. `cargo clippy -p dbt-tasks-sa --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- DuckDB, the repro from #16459 with `dbt seed --full-refresh`: `EVENT_DATE: date` gives `DATE` (was `VARCHAR` on `main` at `759dbee1f`), `event_date: date` still gives `DATE`, and no warning is emitted.

pull_requests.title: state:modified misses inherited changes to grants and other merged configs
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16438

### Problem

Ran into this while poking at Slim CI behavior for grants. The repro in #16438 is solid: with nested directories and inherited `+grants`, flipping an inherited grant from replace (`select: [...]`) to additive (`+select: [...]`) changes the model's effective grants but `state:modified` doesn't select the model, so CD skips it and the warehouse object keeps stale grants.

While reproducing I noticed it's actually broader than the replace-to-additive switch: pretty much any change to grants inherited from an outer directory is missed, even a plain value swap (`select: [role_b]` -> `select: [role_z]`). Only the model's innermost scope is really compared.

The reason: `state:modified` compares `unrendered_config`, and `UnrenderedConfigGenerator._update_from_config` builds that with a flat `result.update()` per fqn level. For merge-behavior fields (grants, meta, tags, pre/post-hook, ...) this keeps only the innermost scope's raw dict, while the effective config accumulates across the whole hierarchy. So an inherited change that alters the effective value but not the innermost raw value is invisible to the comparison.

### Solution

In `_update_from_config`, fold each scope in with `merge_config_dicts` (the dict-level merge already used for config call dicts — handles append/update/dict_key_append and keeps `+` markers intact) instead of the flat update. Scalar fields behave exactly like before (clobber = innermost wins), but merged fields now accumulate across scopes, so an inherited change anywhere in the chain lands in `unrendered_config` and gets compared.

Gated on `state_modified_compare_more_unrendered_values`: with the flag off the legacy flat update is kept as-is. That felt like the right place for it, since the flag already exists to push state comparison towards more unrendered values.

Trade-offs worth calling out:

- One-time effect on upgrade: nodes with inherited merged configs will diff against manifests written by older versions (whose unrendered config only had the innermost scope) and get selected once. Stable after that.
- The expectations in `tests/functional/configs/test_configs_in_schema_files.py` changed for the flag-on case, since unrendered meta/tags now include inherited entries. One quirk surfaced there: `tag_in_schema` shows up twice, because `parser/base.py` deep-merges the rendered patch dict with its unrendered form (which concatenates lists) before building the unrendered config. Left that alone — it's deterministic and pre-existing — and noted it in the fixture.

Verified with a 3-layer project matching the issue (parse, save state, flip layer_2 to additive, then `dbt ls --select state:modified --state`): the model is selected now, and a shadowed outer change that leaves effective grants identical is still (correctly) not selected. Added a functional test covering both of those plus the plain value change. Ran the defer_state, configs, artifacts and previous-version-state functional suites plus the unit tests locally against postgres.

pull_requests.title: fix(databricks): stage V1 view replacements of non-view relations
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16476

Port of databricks/dbt-databricks#1688

### Problem

With `use_materialization_v2` off (the default), when a Databricks view model replaces an existing table or other non-view relation, the view materialization drops the existing relation first and only then creates the view. If the view fails to build, the run fails and the table is already gone.

### Solution

Route that case through `get_replace_sql`, the replacement flow the V2 view path already uses. The view is created at the `__dbt_stg` staging relation first, then swapped in, so a failed build leaves the existing table in place. V1 and V2 now replace a relation of a different type the same way. View-over-view runs keep the existing `create or replace view` path, and grants and tags are applied in the same order as before.

The V1 branch of the vendored `view.sql` matches #1688 byte for byte. The replace-flow macros it calls (`get_replace_sql`, `create_backup`, `execute_multiple_statements`) are already vendored and match current dbt-databricks.

The `dbt-loader` view materialization test for an existing Databricks table now asserts that the first statement creates the view at the staging relation and that the table is renamed out of the way. It fails on `main`, where the view is created directly at the target after the drop.

pull_requests.title: fix(athena): Part 7: Hive column quoting and case folding of quoted identifiers
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16252 (partial)

### Problem

Two dbt-athena behaviours the other Athena parts rely on are missing, and both break a project on its second build:

- `column.quoted_hive` (dbt-athena `AthenaColumn.quoted_hive`, the name in backticks) renders empty. The Hive DDL macros use it (`alter_relation_add_columns` / `_drop_columns` / `_replace_columns` in `column_helpers.sql`), so `on_schema_change: append_new_columns` produces `add columns ( string)`; Athena's Hive parser rejects it and the Trino parser then reports "backquoted identifiers are not supported" for the table name.
- Athena stores every identifier lowercased, quoted or not. `semantic_fqn` keeps the quoted spelling, so the relation cache misses `Lab_MixedCase` (stored as `lab_mixedcase`) and the next build runs a fresh CTAS onto the existing table: `TABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS`.

### Solution

- `Column` exposes `quoted_hive` for Athena only (and enumerates it).
- `BaseRelation::folds_quoted_identifiers`, false by default and true for Athena: `semantic_fqn` normalizes quoted components too.

The two fixes are @aoelvp94's, from his `spike/athena-profile-parse` branch (`215d92513`, and the case-folding part of `c038f2381`), with his authorship; this PR adds the unit tests and the changelog entry.

### Testing

`cargo nextest run -p dbt-adapter -p dbt-schemas` (2182 passed), `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` on both crates. End to end on a real work group with the other Athena parts (#16274, #16376, #16365, #16367, #16368, #16369, #16374, #16370, #16375): a Hive incremental model with `on_schema_change: append_new_columns` gains the new column in Glue on the second run; a model named `Lab_MixedCase` rebuilds with `--full-refresh` onto the existing `lab_mixedcase`; no temporary tables left in Glue.

pull_requests.title: fix: restore node.resource_type.name for dbt 1.x StrEnum compatibility
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16426

### Problem

In dbt 1.x, `node.resource_type` is a Python `StrEnum` — it renders as `"model"` but also exposes `.name` returning `"Model"`. Many custom `generate_database_name` / `generate_schema_name` macros rely on `node.resource_type.name` to get the capitalized member name.

In dbt v2, `resource_type` is serialized as a plain string into the Jinja context. Accessing `.name` on a plain string silently returns empty via minijinja's undefined handling (no error, no warning), causing downstream database/schema targeting logic to silently resolve to the wrong location.

### Solution

Introduce `StrEnumValue` — a minijinja `Object` that renders as the plain string value (`"model"`) but also exposes `.name` (`"Model"`) and `.value` (`"model"`), matching Python `StrEnum` behavior.

Wrap `resource_type` with `StrEnumValue` in all four Jinja context paths:
- Compile context (`compile_node_context.rs`)
- Run context (`run_node_context.rs`)
- Parse context (`resolve_model_context.rs`)
- `generate_*_name` macro args (`utils.rs`)

Also add `NodeType::enum_name()` to return the capitalized variant name.

pull_requests.title: fix: parse inline semantic models declared on versioned models with helper
pull_requests.body:
Resolves dbt-labs/dbt#15294

Supersedes dbt-labs/dbt#15295, which had the right approach but failed the CodeScene "Complex Method" gate and was never updated.

### Problem

An inline (v2) `semantic_model:` on a versioned model is silently dropped, along with its `metrics:`. There is no error or warning, and `dbt sl validate` still reports success.

The versioned branch of `ModelPatchParser.parse_patch` builds a `ParsedNodePatch` per version but never sets `semantic_model`, `metrics`, `derived_semantics`, `agg_time_dimension` or `primary_entity`. `patch_node_properties` then sees `semantic_model=None`, treats it as disabled, and skips it. Unversioned models go through `_get_node_patch`, which does copy those fields.

This happens whether columns are declared under `versions[].columns` or at the top level, because versions inherit top-level columns anyway.

### Solution

Two commits:

1. **Refactor, no behavior change:** extract `NodePatchParser._semantic_patch_fields(target, include=True)`, which returns the five semantic fields as a dict. `_get_node_patch` now uses it instead of five separate assignments.
2. **Fix:** in the versioned loop, pass `**self._semantic_patch_fields(target, include=unparsed_version.v == latest_version)` to the patch. The model-level semantic model resolves through `ref()` to the latest version, so it's attached there only. Attaching it to every version would create duplicates.

Moving the latest-version check into the helper keeps `ModelPatchParser.parse_patch` from getting any more complex. `radon cc` scores:

| | `parse_patch` |
|---|---|
| upstream `1.12.latest` | 22 |
| dbt-labs/dbt#15295 | 27 |
| this PR | 22 |

Not included: `time_spine` is dropped the same way on versioned models. That's a separate follow-up.

### Tests

Two new functional tests in `test_semantic_model_v2_parsing.py`, one with columns under `versions[].columns` and one with top-level columns. Both check that exactly one semantic model is produced, that it depends on `model.test.customers.v2`, that its entity and time dimension are resolved, and that the metric exists. Both fail on unpatched `1.12.latest` with zero semantic models.

Local results (Python 3.11, Postgres 16):
- `tests/unit`: 2055 passed
- `tests/functional/{semantic_models,versions,metrics,partial_parsing}`: 133 passed. One error in `test_pp_vars::TestProfileEnvVars`, which has port 5432 hardcoded while the local DB ran on another port. Unrelated.
- black, isort, flake8 and mypy are clean on the changed files.

pull_requests.title: Fix/15294 signed
pull_requests.body:
Resolves https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt/issues/15294

Extends https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt/pull/15295, which had the right approach but was failing a CodeScene "Complex Method" gate. PR body copied exactly from that PR.

### Problem

An inline (v2) semantic model — and any `metrics:` — declared at the model level on a **versioned** model is silently dropped from the manifest: no error, no warning, and no semantic model or metric is produced. The same definition on a non-versioned model works, and the dbt Fusion (2.0) engine handles the versioned case correctly.

### Root cause

In `PatchParser.parse_patch` (`core/dbt/parser/schemas.py`), the versioned-model branch builds a per-version `ParsedNodePatch` that includes the version's `columns` but omits the model-level semantic constructs (`semantic_model`, `metrics`, `derived_semantics`, `agg_time_dimension`, `primary_entity`) that the non-versioned path sets in `_get_node_patch`. As a result `patch.semantic_model` is always `None`, so `patch_node_properties` never enters the `semantic_model_enabled` branch and `parse_v2_semantic_model_from_dbt_model_patch` / `parse_v2_metrics_from_dbt_model_patch` are never called.

### Fix

Propagate the model-level semantic constructs onto the **latest** version's patch (the version `ref()` resolves to). Gating to the latest version produces exactly one semantic model, rather than zero (the bug) or one per version. Non-versioned parsing is untouched, and versioned models without semantic constructs are unaffected (all fields resolve to `None`, as before).

### How I verified

A minimal project (versioned `cust` + non-versioned `nonvers` control, each with the same inline `semantic_model:` + `metrics:`):

```
# dbt-core 1.12.0-b3 (before)         # with this fix
semantic_models: ['nonvers']          semantic_models: ['cust', 'nonvers']
metrics:         ['nonvers_count']    metrics:         ['cust_count', 'nonvers_count']
```

### Tests / changelog

- Added `TestSemanticModelOnVersionedModel` in `tests/functional/semantic_models/test_semantic_model_v2_parsing.py` (+ fixtures) asserting that a versioned model with an inline semantic model produces exactly one semantic model — with the entity/time-dimension resolved from `versions[].columns` — plus the model-level metric.
- Added a `Fixes` changie entry.

### Notes

- This targets **`1.12.latest`** because `main` is now the Rust/Fusion engine; the bug is specific to the Python 1.x parser (the Fusion engine already parses this correctly). Happy to retarget if there's a preferred branch/process.
- Scoped to the semantic constructs in the report; `time_spine` is intentionally not propagated (a versioned time-spine model isn't a meaningful combination).
- Related: #14600 (same YAML shape, different symptom — a Fusion-engine panic).

There are three problems related to types in unit test fixtures on BigQuery:

pull_requests.title: fix(bigquery): revert list_relations to bulk INFORMATION_SCHEMA query
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16425

### Problem

`list_relations` for BigQuery was migrated to the ADBC driver path in d26a967b5 (preview.206). The BigQuery ADBC driver's `GetObjects` internally issues one sequential `tables.get` API call **per table** in `GetTablesForDBSchema`, turning relation-cache hydration (`hydrate_relation_cache`) into an O(n) round-trip loop. On datasets with 1000+ tables this takes multiple minutes, whereas it was near-instant before the migration.

### Solution

Revert `list_relations()` to call `list_relations_via_information_schema()` directly — a single bulk `SELECT … FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES` query, O(1) regardless of dataset size.

The ADBC code (`list_relations_via_adbc`, `verify_empty_adbc_listing`) is retained as `#[allow(dead_code)]` rather than deleted, so it can be re-enabled once the upstream BigQuery ADBC driver fixes the per-table `Metadata()` call.

### Problem

`dbt source freshness` serialized `sources.json` statuses as `Pass`, `Warn`, and `Error`, while the declared `sources/v3.json` schema only permits lowercase values. Exact-match downstream freshness consumers could therefore reject the artifact or fail to identify warned/error states.

pull_requests.title: [ClickHouse] Populate the relation cache via list_relations
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16427

### Problem

On ClickHouse, `AdapterImpl::list_relations` falls through to the catch-all "not implemented" arm. The Jinja-facing `get_relation` swallows that error, so it can never warm the relation cache for a schema. Every `get_relation` / `load_cached_relation` then runs its own `build_get_relation_sql` query. Each of those scans every `MaterializedView` on the server to build `mvs_pointing_to_it`.

On a ClickHouse Cloud service with ~3.7k tables and ~190 MVs, one project's `dbt run` sent about 500 of these queries at p50 134 ms each. That's roughly 65–70 s of server time per run, plus one round trip per relation. See #16427 for details.

### Solution

Add an `Impl(ClickHouse, engine)` arm to `AdapterImpl::list_relations` that calls the existing `metadata::clickhouse::list_relations`, and remove `ClickHouse` from the catch-all arm. The Fabric, Redshift and DuckDB arms follow the same pattern. `metadata::clickhouse::list_relations` is the bulk `WITH mv_sources AS (...)` listing that `ClickHouseMetadataAdapter::list_relations_in_parallel_inner` already uses. There are no other code changes.

Cached entries carry the same state as the per-relation path. Both `clickhouse::list_relations` and `clickhouse_get_relation` build relations through `with_catalog_state`, so the relation type, `can_exchange`, `mvs_pointing_to_it`, `is_refreshable` and `refreshable_append` all match.

Measured against local ClickHouse 25.4 using `system.query_log`. The project has 26 models across 2 schemas (tables, views and materialized views), with 70 MVs on the server:

| | Run | Per-relation lookups | `mv_sources` listings | SELECTs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 1 (create) | 26 | 0 | 50 |
| `main` | 2 (re-run) | 50 | 0 | 88 |
| this PR | 1 (create) | 0 | 2 | 27 |
| this PR | 2 (re-run) | 0 | 2 | 40 |

Both builds produced the same set of objects in `system.tables`. They also issued identical DDL/DML (57 statements in run 1, 73 in run 2, compared as normalized multisets). A MaterializedView created outside the project, pointing at one of the project's tables, survives the re-run on both builds.

Tradeoffs and notes:

- **Same staleness as dbt 1.x.** The listing is a snapshot of the schema. If an MV is created later in the same invocation pointing at a table that's already cached, that table's cached `mvs_pointing_to_it` won't include it. dbt-clickhouse on dbt 1.x behaves the same way, and the vendored `table.sql` macros already read `mvs_pointing_to_it` from the cached relation.
- **`needs_information` still re-queries.** ClickHouse relations don't set `metadata` in either path, so `get_relation(..., needs_information=True)` bypasses the cache, as it does today. None of the vendored dbt-clickhouse macros pass `needs_information`.
- **Overlap with #16374.** That Athena PR edits the same catch-all arm, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase.

pull_requests.title: Allow integer in filters
pull_requests.body:
Took a Claude stab at resolving #16418 

### Problem

Users using v2 are unable to use Jinja filters where the attribute arg is an integer. See example in #16418 

### Solution

The `map` filter already handled both kinds of argument correctly. I reused its approach rather than writing a new one:

1. **Read `attribute` as any value**, not only a string.
2. **Look it up based on its type** with a shared helper, `get_attr`:
   - a string is looked up by name or dotted path, as before (`"name"`, `"a.0"`)
   - anything else, like an integer, is looked up by position (`0`, `1`)
3. **Use a second helper, `get_attr_or_default`,** for filters that fall back to a default when the lookup fails or finds nothing. It replaces the old `get_path_or_default`, which only took strings; I removed that since nothing uses it any more.

pull_requests.title: fix: don't set legacy type_params.window for v2 cumulative/conversion metrics
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

A v2-spec cumulative metric that declares `window` (rather than `grain_to_date`) fails `dbt parse` with:

```
Cumulative fields `type_params.window` and `type_params.grain_to_date` should be nested under
`type_params.cumulative_type_params.window` and `type_params.cumulative_type_params.grain_to_date`.
```

This is most disruptive when the cumulative metric targets an `input_metric` (rather than a `measure`), since there is no valid nested-YAML workaround in that case — only `require_nested_cumulative_type_params: false` unblocks parsing (downgrading the error to a warning, not fixing anything).

Reported via two customer tickets on Core 1.12 (ZD #135608, #135469).

**Root cause:** `_get_metric_type_params` in `core/dbt/parser/schema_yaml_readers.py` unconditionally copied `UnparsedMetricV2.window` into the legacy, top-level `MetricTypeParams.window` field for every v2 metric. `SemanticManifest.validate()` then treats a truthy `type_params.window` as evidence the metric was written in the deprecated, unnested v1 YAML style and rejects it — even though v2 YAML never has a `type_params` block to begin with. The parser was self-inflicting the error it was checking for.

**Fix:** stop populating that legacy field when parsing v2 metrics. The real window value already lives in `cumulative_type_params.window` / `conversion_type_params.window`, which is unaffected.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `TestCumulativeMetricWithWindowOnInputMetricParsingWorks` (`tests/functional/semantic_models/test_semantic_model_v2_parsing.py`), covering a cumulative metric with `window` on an `input_metric` — the exact shape from the customer reports. Confirmed it fails on the pre-fix code and passes with the fix.
- [x] Full `tests/functional/semantic_models/`, `tests/functional/metrics/`, and related `tests/functional/partial_parsing/` suites pass (84 passed).
- [x] Manually reproduced against a bare project with dbt-core 1.12.3 and confirmed the fix resolves it without needing `require_nested_cumulative_type_params: false`.

pull_requests.title: fix: warn on an exposure depends_on entry that is not ref, source or metric
pull_requests.body:
# Description

Only `ref()`, `source()` and `metric()` register a dependency for an exposure. Every other entry in `depends_on` rendered to nothing and was dropped without a word, so the exposure ended up with no parents at all:

```yaml
depends_on:
  - nonsense('anything_at_all')   # not a thing
  - orders                        # a forgotten ref()
```

`dbt parse` exits 0, `depends_on.nodes` is `[]`, and `dbt ls --select +exposure:dashboard` lists the exposure alone. The failure is silent in exactly the case where the user believes they declared a dependency.

Each entry is now rendered on its own, and an entry that registers no dependency raises a warning naming the entry, the exposure and the file:

```
[WARNING]: Invalid value (nonsense('anything_at_all')) for field depends_on of exposure
'dashboard' in models/schema.yml, which must call ref(), source() or metric()
```

It goes through `fire_or_defer_event(..., force_warn_or_error_handling=True)`, so `--warn-error` turns it into an error.

**On warning vs. error:** the v2 engine already rejects these entries outright, with the same rule (`crates/dbt-jinja-utils/src/utils.rs`: *"Exposure depends_on entry `{}` does not call ref(), source(), or metric()"*). I kept 1.x at a warning because failing the parse on a line that silently worked before is a breaking change on a stable line, and the issue asks for "parsing fails, or at least warns". If you would rather have parity with v2 here, it is a one-line change and I am happy to make it.

# Related Issue(s)

- closes #16380

# Tests

Two tests in `tests/unit/parser/test_parser.py` (`SchemaParserExposureTest`):

- `test_unrecognized_depends_on_entry_warns`: both an unknown function and a bare model name produce a warning each, and the exposure has no refs or sources. Fails on `1.latest`.
- `test_supported_depends_on_entries_do_not_warn`: `ref()` and `source()` entries produce no warning and still register as dependencies. Passes before and after, so it guards against a false positive.

`pytest tests/unit` is green (2190 passed, 10 skipped). `black`, `isort`, `flake8` and `mypy --show-error-codes` are clean on the changed files.

pull_requests.title: fix: keep the microbatch event-time filter on relations derived from a ref
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16383

### Problem

In a microbatch model, a relation derived from a ref, such as `{{ ref('x').include(...) }}`, drops the batch's event-time filter, so each batch reads the whole upstream table while the delete only covers the batch window. dbt Core keeps the filter.

`RelationObject::call_method` re-wraps the derived relation with `RelationObject::new`, which resets `run_filter` and `event_time`.

### Solution

`include`, `quote`, `replace_path`, `incorporate` and `without_identifier` now re-wrap through a helper that keeps the filter, matching dbt v1. `derivative`, `create_from` and `information_schema` point at a different object and are unchanged.

Tested with a `jinja_assert` test covering all five (it fails without the fix) and end to end on Snowflake, running microbatch models over a 2-day window of a 10-day source:

| Model reads | 2.0.6 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `ref('src')` | 2 rows | 2 rows |
| `ref('src').include(database=false)` | 19 rows | 2 rows |
| `ref('src').quote(...)` | 19 rows | 2 rows |
| `ref('src').replace_path(identifier=...)` | 19 rows | 2 rows |
| `ref('src').incorporate(path=...)` | 19 rows | 2 rows |

`without_identifier()` has no table to read, so it is covered by the unit test only.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read [the contributing guide](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and understand what's expected of me.
- [x] I have run this code in development, and it appears to resolve the stated issue.
- [x] This PR includes tests, or tests are not required or relevant for this PR.
- [x] This PR has no interface changes (e.g., macros, CLI, logs, JSON artifacts, config files, adapter interface, etc.) or this PR has already received feedback and approval from Product or DX.

pull_requests.title: feat: add write-audit-publish for Snowflake table builds
pull_requests.body:
### Problem

A table-model build can expose transformed data before its data tests pass.
This feature is narrowly scoped to `dbt build` for Snowflake SQL models materialized as tables.

### Solution

Opt-in `wap=true` builds and audits a unique same-schema working table, then clones it to the public target only after every required audit passes.
Ordinary downstream refs continue to read the published table until its replacement passes the required audits.

### Table cleanup

Working tables are permanent/transient tables in the same schema. dbt explicitly drops them after successful publication, or after all model tasks and audits finish on failure; cleanup only targets tables this invocation confirmed it created.
`wap_retain_failed=true` keeps failed candidates. Crashes, cancellation, uncertain publication, or cleanup errors can leave tables behind; older retained tables are not swept.

### Validation

Added to the rust and python test harness along with running this build against our snowflake db
```
version: 2

models:
  - name: wap_demo
    description: Local-only WAP demonstration model for dbt PR #16384.
    columns:
      - name: col_a
        description: Audit key; the failing scenario intentionally sets this to NULL.
        data_type: NUMBER
        tests:
          - not_null
          - unique
      - name: col_b
        description: Demonstrates the value that is atomically published.
        data_type: VARCHAR

```

```
{{
    config(
        materialized='table',
        wap=var('wap_enabled', false),
        wap_retain_failed=var('wap_retain_failed', false),
        pre_hook=[],
        post_hook=[],
        snowflake_warehouse=auto_scale_model(),
    )
}}

{% if var('wap_fail', false) %}
    SELECT
        CAST(NULL AS number) AS col_a
        , 'intentional-audit-failure' AS col_b
{% else %}
    SELECT
        1 AS col_a
        , 'published-by-wap' AS col_b
{% endif %}

```

pull_requests.title: fix: preserve docs lineage hop counts across expansion
pull_requests.body:
Resolves #16379

### Problem

Selecting `3+` / `+6` in the inline docs DAG and clicking **Expand** resets both controls to `1+` / `+1`. Closing the expanded view also loses its hop selections. The lens survives because it uses shared state, while each DAG initializes its hop controls locally.

### Solution

Initialize each DAG's hop controls from the existing lineage store when its root matches the requested resource. This preserves upstream and downstream selections, including `max`, across expansion and closing. A different root still starts at `1+` / `+1`, including when recentering an already-mounted DAG.

Includes browser regression stories, a changie-generated changelog entry, and rebuilt `web/dist/` assets so the fix ships in the dbt binary.

### Validation

- The Expand regression failed against the original code at the missing `3+` control and passes with the fix.
- 17 browser tests passed across the inline, expanded, and base DAG stories, including Expand/Close and different-root reset coverage.
- 13 lineage store/data-hook unit tests passed.
- Scoped ESLint, `pnpm build` (TypeScript and Vite), built asset reference checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
